title: main does not build its tests: posting_section_mode.rs test builds Tilt without basis_version (#2157 x #2245)

labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: in-review

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

body:
## What fails

`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets` (and the debug test build) on upstream/main `2b7a8950d` and later:

```
error[E0063]: missing field `basis_version` in initializer of `operation::types::params::Tilt`
   --> crates/app/src/posting_section_mode.rs:133:35
```

## Cause

Two PRs that each built alone, merged in sequence on 2026-11-16 without a combined test:
- PR #2157 (`81f24951e`) added the required field `Tilt::basis_version`.
- PR #2245 (`2b7a8950d`) added a unit test in `posting_section_mode.rs` with a `Tilt` literal of the old shape.

Test code only. Product code builds. Found by mkinney's hourly main health check.

## Fix

Add `basis_version: 1` to the literal (the value of every other new `Tilt` literal, for example in `operation/frame.rs` and `tests/area_controls.rs`).

Done means: the all-targets clippy and the `posting_section_mode` unit tests are green on main.

title: 2D contour and slot ladders: check the entry at solid pass starts after #2265

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Follow-up of #2265.

The fix for #2265 adds a rule to `pass_link` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`). When the user asks for a helix, ramp or arc entry, a pass start in material gets that entry, or a named stand-in. Only the pocket family (Pocket, rest 2D, Adaptive) opts in, through `Motion::with_solid_restart()` in `pocket_emit.rs`.

The other planar ladders (2D contour, slot, trace) do not opt in. Their pass starts use the existing entry laws.

To find:
- Can a contour, slot or trace ladder start a pass (not the first pass of a level) in material with a centre-cutting tool, when the user asked for a helix or ramp?
- If yes, file it as a defect by the AGENTS.md priority table, and opt that ladder in with its own pinning test and golden review.

Done means: each planar ladder either opts in, or a test shows that its pass starts in material do not occur.

`crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` (`FieldPlay`, `PlayIndex`) and `crates/app/src/stock_play_worker.rs` (`PlayWorker`) hold domain logic. They cut the stock and serve the playback pictures. Only `PlaySeed::gather` and `FieldPlay::new` read the ECS world.

AGENTS.md "app holds the document, nothing else" puts this code in the simulation crate.

## Context

The review of PR #2192 (issue #2181) found the same rule for the new keyframe code. That PR moved the keyframe store and the calculation loop to `camcraft_sim::play_keys` and `camcraft_sim::play_precalc`. The methods of `FieldPlay` and `PlayWorker` stayed in app, because these types are in app. They existed before #2181.

## Done means

- `FieldPlay`, `PlayIndex`, `PlayWorker` and their head and precalc methods are in `camcraft-sim`.
- `PlaySeed::gather` (the world read) stays in app. App re-exports the moved items.
- The rotary and lathe cut helpers that `FieldPlay::cut` calls are reachable from sim, or are passed in.
- The playback suites (`stock_play`, `stock_play_partial`, `stock_play_precalc`, `stock_view`) pass unchanged.
- No change to the picture, the Deviate verdict or the post gate.

title: 2D Adaptive: only the first region gets the helix entry; each other entry is a straight plunge into material, with no warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16, with two screenshots (build `v0.22.0 · f6c7f605`, a local test build):

> "Bug in 2D Adapive. This was generated by setting a stock boundary and picking the outside edge of the part. I will helix down the first hole and clearing it out all the other Entrys inside and outside the part is missing lead ins of same helix setting. Same issue if i remove the boundary.. Only a helix leadin on the first pocket.. not the secondd one. This kinda comes back to how containment is getting interpreted... But problem ppeprsista even if i pick two inside faces of the pockets.. Helix is only on the first pocket, second is justa straight plunge into the material with no warning."

What happens:

- Project `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`), 2D Adaptive, tool `EM-0800-4FL` (8 mm end mill), post Fanuc (built-in).
- Lead in / Lead out page: Entry Type `Helix`, Helix radius 1.6 mm, Minimum radius, pitch and angle on Auto, Plunge enabled.
- The operation generates: "8832 moves (27 plunge(s) @ 300, 3 level(s), 2286 arc(s)), 12 warning(s)".
- The first pocket gets the helix entry. Each other entry, inside and outside the part, is a straight plunge into the material.
- No warning names the plunges.
- The result is the same for three selections: stock boundary with the outside edge; no boundary; the two inside faces of the pockets.

Expected:

- Each entry into material uses the selected entry type (helix), at each region and each level.
- Where the helix does not fit, the ramp comes next. A straight plunge into material is the last fallback only.
- Each entry that falls back gets a warning that names the region, the level and the reason. The page says "where the helix cannot fit, a ramp and then a plunge stand in": the user must see when this happens.
- A plunge into material with a tool that cannot cut at its centre is refused or blocks the post, by the rule that the project has for such tools.
- A plunge in open air (outside the stock, or in an area that an earlier pass cleared) needs no helix and no warning.

To find:

1. Why the entry planner gives the helix to the first region only. Does it try the helix for each region, or one time for the operation?
2. If the 27 plunges are in material or in cleared area, by the stock state at that moment.
3. If the Offset rings fallback is the cause. The status line says "the HSM plan is refused: the area is a channel 10.6 mm wide ..."; the fallback path possibly does not apply the entry settings.
4. Why no warning is made.

Safety: a straight plunge into uncut material without a warning is wrong output that can break a tool. The fix changes posted G-code of 2D Adaptive (entry moves) and is under the safety floor. The verify check and the post gate do not become weaker. No real control run exists.

Related: #2232 (containment Outside, option 1 selected), and the "feed moves cross in XY at shared depth" warnings on this project (seen in the review of PR #2214).

Done means: a test on a part with two separate pockets (and one with an outside region) asserts a helix or ramp entry at each region and level where it fits, and a named warning for each entry that falls back to a plunge in material. The goldens that change are named in the PR.

title: Debug info: log the frame rate when it changes, and make the debug info panel dockable

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16. The maintainer set the priority `P2` in his own words:

> "Issue; p2; Log framerate to debug info as a value when it changes in performance once - and if it keeps jumping around log just every 10s or something like that.. Make debug info "dockable" as well."

Wanted, part 1 - frame rate in the debug info:

- The debug info shows the frame rate (and the frame time in ms) as a value.
- When the frame rate changes to a different level, the debug info logs one line with the new value. Use a threshold, so that small noise logs nothing.
- When the frame rate does not become stable, the debug info logs at most one line each 10 s. That line gives the minimum, the maximum and the mean of the interval.
- An idle application that does not repaint logs nothing.

Wanted, part 2 - dockable debug info:

- The user can dock the debug info panel as the other panels dock, and can undock it again.
- The dock position is part of the saved layout.

Rules:

- The measurement costs no work in proportion to the model. It reads the frame times that the application has (frame cost rule, #2238). The log does not request a repaint.
- The log rate limit applies to the `gpu: slow frame` lines too, or the issue says why not.
- Panel layout is ephemeral UI state, not a command.
- The text is plain English.

Done means: a unit test pins the log rule (one line for one level change; no more than one line each 10 s when the value moves; no line when idle); a structural test pins that the debug info panel is present docked and undocked; the PR has before and after screenshots.

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16:

> "while generating a toolpath a "progress" bar should overlay the view port."

What happens: while an operation generates its toolpath, the viewport shows no progress. The user cannot see that the work runs, how far it is, or which operation it is.

Expected: while one or more generate jobs run, a progress bar lies over the viewport.

- It names the operation that generates.
- It shows the progress. Where the generator reports no fraction, it shows an activity bar and the elapsed time.
- It goes away when the job ends, is refused or is cancelled. A refusal still shows its message as it does today.
- With more than one job, it shows the count ("2 of 5") and the current operation.
- The text is plain English, with no G-code terms.

Rules:

- The bar is ephemeral UI state: it is not a command and it is not in the undo history.
- It reads the state of the generate jobs. It starts no work and it does not block the UI thread.
- It obeys the frame cost rule of #2238: an unchanged frame does no work in proportion to the model, and the bar requests a repaint only while a job runs.
- It changes no toolpath and no posted G-code.

Done means: a structural test (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs` family) pins that the bar is present with the operation name while a job runs and is absent after the job ends or is refused; the PR has before and after screenshots.

title: Process: test merge batches before they reach main, and make a release cut take about an hour (v0.22.0 took about 6 h)

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Asked for by the maintainer's collaborator (2026-11-16, after the v0.22.0 cut): "This should be smooth and quick. Pull all processing before the merge to main if possible. Velocity Velocity Velocity". These are proposals for the maintainer to decide. Nothing here changes a process file yet.

## What happened on 2026-11-16

| Phase | Time | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| Merge stop to release branch | about 3.5 h | `main` did not compile (#2143, from #1753), a red test (#2137), a P1 found during the cut (#2152), and a P2 with two competing fix PRs (#2004: #2013 and #2141) |
| Release gate (`cut.yml`) | 1.6 h | the full release tier in one job on one runner |
| Merge, tag, `release.yml` | about 1 h | package builds on hosted runners |

Later the same day `main` went red two more times (#2198, #2244). Each time, two PRs that passed alone did not build or pass together (#2244: #2140 and #2077). The post-merge gate found each one, but only after the merge.

## Proposals

1. **Test the batch before the merge (a merge queue).** Before a merge batch, build a candidate: `main` plus every PR of the batch, merged in the `merge-plan` order. Run the batch tier on the candidate. Merge the batch only when the candidate is green. If it is red, remove the PR that breaks it and test again. The post-merge gate then only confirms. (mkinney's coordinator does this on its own machines from today, with the user's yes for each PR.)
2. **Check `main` on each new commit.** A fast compile check (clippy on all crates, `--all-targets`) and `cargo test -p xtask` take about 2 to 5 minutes with a warm cache. A failure names the merge within the hour. (mkinney's coordinator runs this hourly from today; it found #2244.)
3. **A cut-readiness verdict before "cut".** Before the merge stop: no open P1 or P2, no open release PR, the compile check and the batch tier green on that exact `main` sha, and the packaging dry run green. The result is one line: GO or NO-GO with the reasons.
4. **Reuse a green rehearsal at the cut.** Run the release tier nightly on `main`. If `release/vX.Y.Z` differs from a rehearsed sha only by release notes, `CHANGELOG.md`, `RECOMMENDED.md` and the version bump, `cut.yml`'s gate stage accepts the rehearsal result (the same "gated tree is the tagged tree" check that the tag stage makes). Saves about 1.5 h.
5. **Split the release tier across runners.** The heavy lanes are independent. Run them as parallel jobs on the self-hosted runners (uma, m3 and others), then join the results. About 1.6 h becomes about 30 min when a full run is necessary.
6. **Measure `release.yml`.** Find the slowest job (probably macOS) and check the cache and split options.
7. **One fix for one P1/P2.** No second fix PR for an issue that already has one, and a known gap in a P1/P2 fix is fixed on the branch, not left as a note (the cause of #2152).

Target: a cut from GO to published release in about 1 hour, and `main` green between cuts.

## Open questions for the maintainer

- Accept 1 for all collaborator merges (the repository `merge-ready` skill would build and test the candidate before it merges)?
- Accept 4 and 5 for `cut.yml` (a process change, with a `PROCESS_VERSION` bump)?
- Which runner runs the nightly rehearsal (3 and 4)?

Done means: the maintainer decides each proposal on this issue, and each accepted one gets its own sub-issue.

body:
Part of #2238 (frame cost: calculate before and cache). Measured with the frame-cost probe of #2238, release build, fig8.step.

## What happens

`interact::selection_feature_lines` (`crates/ui/src/interact.rs`) makes the overlay lines of the shown picks on each scene collection. It reads the operation from the world and calls `feature_lines` for each pick each time.

| State | Piece | ms per frame (release) |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Adaptive on one welded face | `scene/overlay.selection_features` | 1.48 |
| 2D Adaptive on one welded face | `ui/viewport.pick_ink` | 0.96 |

## Done means

- The overlay lines are made when the shown picks or the model change, and read from a cache on other frames. The cache is in a `ui` module next to `selection_feature_lines` (for example `frame_memo`), not in a widget.
- The key follows `docs/decisions/2238-frame-cost-rule.md`: the pick list value and the `Arc` of the model features.
- A counter test: a still frame makes zero new line sets.
- A changed-input test: a new pick gives new lines, equal to a fresh calculation.
- The probe `frame_cost_probe` shows the piece under 0.1 ms in release.

body:
What happens: the maintainer ran the test build of PR #2243 (`camcraft-2235-367f48185.exe`, v0.22.0 · 9695ea08) on `testdata/models/fig8.camproj`. Edge selection is fast now. But when the operation shows its filled area preview (the orange band outside the part, 2D Adaptive, Containment `Outside`, a welded face of 424 strips selected), the frame rate drops.

The words of the maintainer, 2026-11-16: "2235, selecting eddges performs well.. that "visualized" outside area in orange tho.. It dropped framerate"

Evidence (his log):

```
WARN generate{op=2D Adaptive1}: camcraft_app::operation::generate::run_job: generation refused: invalid machining parameters: adaptive: the center area has no room for an entry kind=2D Adaptive ms=72
gpu: slow frame 201 ms (budget 100 ms, 1 slow so far) - slowest phase "commands" 94 ms [commands 94 ms, scene 22 ms, ui 84 ms, acquire 0 ms, encode 0 ms, submit+present 0 ms]
```

The slow phases are `commands` (94 ms) and `ui` (84 ms), not `scene`. The log has one slow frame at the moment of the refused generate. The maintainer reports a lower frame rate while the band shows. The cause is not known: find it with a measurement before a fix.

Expected: a frame with the area preview on screen stays under 10 ms when nothing changed (target of #2235 and #2238). The area fill is derived data: compute it one time for each change of its inputs and cache the mesh.

Related: #2235 / PR #2243 (selected-chain frame cost; this work stacks on that branch), #2201 (hover path, a different claim), #2232 (the refusal "no room for an entry" itself), #2238 (cache strategy).

Not in scope: the refusal text and the entry strategy (#2232). The area that the preview shows and the cut geometry must not change.

Done means: a test pins that a frame without a change builds no area fill and runs no generate-side work; the measured cost of the `commands` and `ui` phases with the preview shown is in the PR; the maintainer has a test build.

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-16:

> "caching to not have to redraw things should prob. be a strategy thru out the application to keep framerates stable and enough compute lefter over for things that matter.. Precalculation and cache is not something that will give us a penalty.. this is not game engine"

and, for the frame time: "the performance needs to gget down under 10ms to be useable".

What is wanted: one strategy for the full application. A frame does not calculate again what did not change. Derived data (chains, stitched rings, overlay geometry, panel rows, meshes, simulation views) is calculated one time, stored, and made invalid by a change of its inputs. A wait for a calculation before the display is acceptable.

Today: #2201, #2209 and #2235 each repair one place where a frame does work in proportion to the model or the selection. Each repair has its own cache and its own invalidation rule.

Work, in this order:

1. Measure. List the work that each frame does in `commands`, `scene` and `ui` on a large model (`fig8.step` and one larger), with a probe that stays in the test suite.
2. Design one cache rule: the key (a model revision, a selection revision, a document revision), who makes an entry invalid, and where the entries are stored (app layer, not UI widgets). Record it in `docs/decisions/` and in `crates/ui/AGENTS.md`.
3. Idle frames: when no input and no change exists, the app does not repaint, or it repaints from stored buffers.
4. Move each measured hot path to the rule, one sub-issue for each.
5. A budget test: a frame without a change is below 10 ms on the reference models. The gate runs it.

Safety: a cache must never show or cut stale geometry. Each cache has a test that a change of its inputs makes it invalid. The verify check and the post gate read the document, not a display cache.

Done means: the decision is recorded, the budget test is in the gate, and the sub-issues for the measured hot paths are filed. #2235 gives the first cache and the first probe.

body:
Add an external NC program simulation runner and command in `crates/app`.
It connects `camcraft-gcode` (#2217) to CamCraft's stock simulation, collision verification, and machine limit checks.

## Scope
- Depend on `camcraft-gcode` in `crates/app/Cargo.toml` and record the crate edge in `docs/decisions/` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Map each `T<n>` number from the NC file to a document tool (`tool_numbers::numbers` in `crates/app/src/tool_numbers.rs`), a `.camtools` file (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`), or an explicit `T -> tool` map.
- Return the list of unmapped `T<n>` numbers and refuse simulation when any `T` number lacks cutter geometry.
- Read stock, optional target models, fixtures, WCS origins (`G54`..`G59`), and the mounted `.mch` from the active setup (`crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs`, `crates/app/src/setup_wcs.rs`), while allowing caller overrides.
- Transform NC program coordinates into world millimeters (`world = origin + sign * program_mm`), reversing `posting::wcs_context` and `post::invert` (`crates/post/src/post/invert.rs`).
- Run `camcraft_sim::stock_sim::Dexel` and `deviate` against the setup stock and optional target model, refusing setups with no stock by name (`stock_sim::stock_grid`).
- Run region-free verification laws: `verify::solid_hits` against the target model (when present), `bands_vs_fixtures_held`, and `rapids_vs_fixtures_held` (`crates/sim/src/verify/laws.rs`, `solid.rs`).
- Run `machine::judge` travel, feed, and spindle checks (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`), mapping every finding to its 1-based NC line number.
- Build a `PlaySeed` (`crates/app/src/stock_play.rs`) for the parsed sections so UI playback can run it.

Depends on #2217.

Done means: Integration tests in `crates/app/tests/` simulate a 3-axis NC file against stock, model, fixtures, and `.mch`, refuse unmapped tools or missing stock by name, return line-numbered gouge/fixture/travel findings, and construct a working `PlaySeed`.

body:
Create the pure-Rust crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`) beside `crates/post`.
It parses RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556) and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections (`crates/cl/src/cl/path.rs`) and a 1-based line map.

## Scope
- Depend only on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry`, and `thiserror` (no `boa_engine`, no `flecs_ecs`, no `camcraft-post` dependency).
- Record the new `camcraft-cl` and `camcraft-geometry` crate edges in `docs/decisions/` per `AGENTS.md`.
- Accept dialect configuration and optional machine reference positions from the caller.
- Track modal groups: motion (`G0`, `G1`, `G2`, `G3`, `G80`), plane (`G17`, `G18`, `G19`), distance (`G90`, `G91`), arc center (`G90.1`, `G91.1`), feed mode (`G94`), units (`G20`, `G21`), length offset (`G43 H`, `G49`), work offsets (`G54`..`G59`), and cycle return (`G98`, `G99`).
- Parse `I`/`J`/`K` arcs and `R` radius arcs (`R > 0` minor arc, `R < 0` major arc) in XY, XZ, and YZ planes.
- Expand canned cycles (`G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G86`, `G89`) into explicit `cl::Move` chains (`crates/sim/src/sim.rs`).
- Handle `T`, `M6`, `S`, `M3`/`M4`/`M5`, `M0`/`M1`/`M2`/`M30`, `G4`, `G61`/`G64`, and `G53`/`G28`/`G30` when reference positions exist.
- Split sections on tool changes and record a 1-based source line number for every move.
- Refuse unknown words, missing unit mode, `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, and `A`/`B`/`C` words by name with the 1-based line number.
- Add a clean-room provenance comment to each module (`AGENTS.md`).

Done means: `camcraft-gcode` builds in the workspace with a `docs/decisions/` entry, parses 3-axis ISO programs into `cl::Toolpath` sections with a 1-based line map, and tests pin modal tracking, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs, canned cycles, unit scaling, and named line-numbered refusals.

Part of #2213

body:
Asked on Discord (2026-11-16): "Are we going to do a trajectory simulation? Something like CAMotics?" The maintainer's collaborator wants it: "Yes open ticket, I would like that".

## What is missing

CamCraft simulates the toolpaths that it generates: stock removal, playback, and the tool, holder, fixture and machine-travel laws (#2181, #2193, #2194 improve the playback). It cannot open a G-code file and simulate it. Examples of files that users want to check:
- a program from a different CAM program;
- a hand-written or edited program;
- a CamCraft program that was edited after the post.

## Wanted

Open an `.nc` / `.tap` / `.gcode` file, select the machine (and with it the dialect), and simulate it with the existing stock simulation and verify laws: material removal, gouges against an optional model, collisions with the holder and fixtures, and travel limits. The result is the same view and the same findings as for CamCraft's own toolpaths.

## Open questions (research)

1. **Reader.** A G-code reader for each supported dialect (Fanuc, Haas, Tormach/LinuxCNC, grblHAL, Heidenhain conversational, Siemens, Mazak, Doosan, Sodick wire...). Which words are read: modal groups, G90/G91, G20/G21, arcs (I/J/K and R), planes G17/G18/G19, canned cycles (expanded to moves), tool changes (T/M6 and the tool length offset), work offsets, G28/G30/G53, subprograms and macros. What is refused by name.
2. **Tools.** How a file's tool numbers map to CamCraft tools: the machine's tool table, the document's tool library, or a prompt for each T number.
3. **Setup.** Stock, work offset and fixtures: taken from the open document, or entered with the file.
4. **Multi-axis.** 4th and 5th axis words, through the machine kinematics (the AC solver of #2056 in reverse).
5. **Units and errors.** A word that the reader does not understand gives a clear refusal with the line number, never a silent skip.
6. **Use of it.** A "compare" mode: post a CamCraft program, then read it back and simulate it, so that the post is checked end to end (a round-trip test for every built-in post).
7. **Where it lives.** A reader crate beside `camcraft-post` (domain only), with the open-file command and its MCP tool in `app`.

## Clean room

Specify the reader from public sources only: the G-code standards (RS-274/NGC, ISO 6983), the controls' published programming manuals, and our own post scripts. Do not read or adapt the code of CAMotics, LinuxCNC's interpreter or other G-code simulators. Do not use programs that Fusion 360 or HSMWorks generated as test input.

## Done means

The open questions are answered in comments on this issue, and the concrete sub-issues are filed (each with one `P*`, one `effort:*`, `area:*`, `source:agent`, a "Done means" line and "Part of #N"), linked back here. Then `needs-research` is dropped and this umbrella closes.

title: 2D Adaptive refuses to generate in a setup that holds the part turned: "area controls are not supported yet in an aligned setup"

labels.name: bug

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16, build v0.22.0 `ef1f5345`; filed by an agent. The maintainer set the priority:

> "Bug, P1; 2D Adaptive; generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - area controls are not supported yet in an aligned setup"

## What happens

1. Open `testdata/models/fig8.camproj` (model `fig8.step`, vise fixture, stock, tool `EM-0800-4FL`, one 2D Adaptive). The files are in the maintainer's checkout (see #2209).
2. `Setup1` holds the part turned (part alignment).
3. The 2D Adaptive has an edge chain selection on the Geometry tab.
4. Click Generate.

Result: no toolpath. The message is:

```
generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Adaptive1: invalid machining parameters: setup 'Setup1' holds the part turned (part alignment) - area controls are not supported yet in an aligned setup
```

## Expected

A 2D Adaptive generates in an aligned setup, with its area selection. A part that is turned onto the vise is a usual setup, and a 2D Adaptive is the usual first roughing operation.

## Facts for the fix

- The refusal is deliberate ("not supported yet"). It is not a crash and it does not give a wrong toolpath. The work is to supply the missing behaviour, not to remove the guard.
- The area controls (the picked chain or face, the boundary) must go through the part alignment transform into the setup frame, with the same transform that the model and the stock use.
- Find each operation that has the same refusal (search for the message text) and list them on this issue. Fix them with one shared transform, or file one issue for the others.
- The message does not tell the user what to do. If a case stays refused, the message names the control to clear.

## Safety

The fix is under the safety floor: it changes where the tool cuts in an aligned setup. A wrong transform (sign, order or pivot) cuts in the wrong place.

- Pin with a setup where the part is turned 90 degrees and the area is not symmetric, so that a wrong frame gives a different region.
- The verify check and the post gate judge the result against the turned part and the stock.
- Do not remove the refusal before the transform has its tests.

Done means: `fig8.camproj` generates its 2D Adaptive in the aligned setup; a test pins the cut region against the turned part; each other operation with this refusal is fixed or has its own issue.

title: Edge picking: the edge below a chamfer on a swept wall is many 0.9 mm pieces, not one edge (fig8.step)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16, build v0.22.0 `ef1f5345`; filed by an agent:

> "the model imported (fig8.step in testdata) - has chamfer so the edge below the chamfer look like this ... an enormous amount of small sections rather than a welded edge like the one above."

## What happens

1. Import `fig8.step`. The model has a swept (figure-eight) wall with a chamfer at its top.
2. Add a 2D Adaptive. On the Geometry tab set "Click selects" to Edges.
3. Click the upper edge of the chamfer. The pick is one edge: `Chain fig8 · open · 113.1 mm · 1 of 1`.
4. Click the edge below the chamfer (chamfer to wall). Each click picks a piece of about 0.9 mm. Four Ctrl+clicks give `Chain fig8 · open · 0.9 mm · 1 of 4` to `4 of 4`.

## Expected

The edge below the chamfer is one feature edge, as the edge above it is. One click picks its full length. A chain made from it has one row.

## Why it matters

- The user cannot select this edge for a 2D operation in practice: an edge of about 113 mm needs more than 100 clicks.
- A chain of many short open pieces can give a toolpath with many short moves, or a refusal, where one smooth chain is correct.
- The rule of #692 says that only feature edges are pickable, never tessellation edges. These pieces look like tessellation or patch joints that the pick shows as feature edges.

## Where to look

- Find if the STEP file has this edge as many short edges (a chamfer made of many small faces), or if the kernel import or `decompose` splits one curve.
- If the file has many short edges that are tangent-continuous: join them to one pickable feature edge at import or at the pick (G1 chain below an angle limit).
- If the import splits one curve: keep the curve as one edge.
- Compare with the upper chamfer edge of the same model, which is one edge.

Workaround: Shift+click picks the whole loop, where the loop is the wanted geometry.

Safety floor: the change is in model geometry or its edge topology, which feeds chains and toolpaths. Thus `effort:high`.

Related: #692 (feature edges only), #1505 (edge picking), #2201 (slow frames while an edge is selected, same model and session).

Done means: on `fig8.step`, one click on the edge below the chamfer picks the full edge as one chain row, and a test on that file pins the edge count of the chamfer's lower boundary.

body:
Reported by a user on Discord (f1inch), relayed by the maintainer's collaborator on 2026-11-16; filed by an agent:

> "after i add a second operation after faceing the camcraft gets so damn slow that i cant work with it."

The user shared the project privately. It is not attached here.

## The project (shape only)

- Project version 61, 17 MB on disk.
- One model of about 45,000 triangles (8.4 MB of facets).
- One setup, one box stock, one tool (4 mm router bit).
- Two operations: `Face1`, then `2D Contour1`.
- Machine: a hobby router file (FoxAlien WM-3020), grblHAL post.

## Readings (headless, release build of main 3580f3888, Linux)

| Step | Time |
|---|---|
| `open_project` | 0.1 s |
| `generate` 2D Contour1 (forced) | 1.0 s |
| `generate` Face1 (forced) | < 0.1 s |
| `verify` | 0.2 s |

So project load, generation and verification are fast. The slowness is in the windowed shell: the redraw, the scene rebuild, the toolpath or stock display, or the simulation. #164 (closed) found a similar pattern: one CPU core at 100% in the window while `camcraft-cli process` took under a second.

The project also has two problems that are not this defect:
- The model was saved before mesh fidelity was recorded (v58 or older), so the gouge check blocks the post until the model is imported again.
- `Face1` moves go outside the machine stroke (X to -47.5, Z to -4, stroke X 0..290, Z 0..70): 626 limit problems.

A large number of findings can make a UI list slow. Check if the window rebuilds or paints all 626 findings each frame.

## What is not known yet

- Which action is slow: select an operation, regenerate, rotate the view, or play the simulation.
- The user's CamCraft version, operating system and GPU (the paths suggest Linux).
- If one operation is fast and two operations are slow.

## Done means

On a fixture with the same shape (a model of about 45,000 triangles, a Face and a 2D Contour, and several hundred findings), the windowed UI stays responsive: a frame cost close to the one-operation case, no CPU core held at 100% when idle. A test pins the cost that caused it (for example the scene or findings rebuild count for each frame).

title: Tool body: a holder drawn beside the shank widens the whole judged shank, so the reach check and verify refuse legal 3D ops

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #1749 (the user's `sc_logo.camproj`). Related to #2180 (a band that only touches the shank top). This case is wider: the holder band starts below the stated shank top, beside the shank.

## What happens

The tool T31 has `shank_d` 6.35 (the same as the cutter). Its drawn holder body starts 38.1 mm above the tip. The stated shank top is 65.278 mm. So the holder band stands beside the shank from 38.1 to 65.278 mm.

`tool_body::judged` calls `HolderProfile::enclose` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`). `enclose` widens the whole judged shank, from the flute top (14.478 mm) upward, to the band diameter (35 mm).

Results on the user's project (forced regeneration, main `ce59ef446`):
- The #1844 reach preflight refuses "S1 Notch adaptive + terrace finish". The refusal is false.
- `verify` reports false `shank_hit` findings on four ops: 8138, 6884, 479 and 219 findings. They hold the post.

## Expected

The judged body follows the drawn tool: the shank stays Ø6.35 below the holder foot. The holder band counts only where it is (from 38.1 mm up). A real holder collision must still be found and must still hold the post.

## Why it matters

The refusal is safe, but it is wrong. The user cannot post a legal program. This blocks `sc_logo.camproj` from a clean post, whatever happens with #1749.

## Safety

Do not make the judged body smaller than the real tool anywhere. Pin both directions:
- the false refusal goes away for a holder above the reach;
- a holder band that does reach the stock still gives `shank_hit` / holder findings and holds the post.

Done means: on a fixture like T31 (shank Ø6.35, holder from 38.1 mm, shank top 65.278 mm), the reach preflight and verify judge the shank at Ø6.35 below 38.1 mm; a test with a holder that touches the stock still refuses; #2180's case is checked too.

body:
## What happens

A closed 2D Contour with an exit point (#1473) whose overlap runs past a rounded corner generates `ok`, but `verify` blocks it with crossing findings and the post is refused:

```
post: post blocked - 18 warning(s): C1: feed moves 5 and 15 cross in XY at shared depth; C1: feed moves 5 and 17 cross in XY at shared depth; ...
```

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate (z 0 to 10) with a 30 × 20 × 5 pocket, as a closed, outward-wound ASCII STL. The outside contour runs at offset 3 with r 3 arcs at the four corners.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "plate2.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 70, "dy": 50, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "contour", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "C1", "source": "plate2",
   "params": {"top_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": -3, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "stepdown": 3,
              "links": {"approach": {"start_point": [30, 0], "exit_point": [0, -20]}}}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "C1"}], ["verify", {}], ["post", {"output": "c1.nc"}]]
```

The moves of the first level, read from the cached toolpath in a throwaway test:

```
  3 Feed (33,8) -> (33,0)                     lead-in to the start point
  4 Feed (33,0) -> (33,-20)
  5 Feed (33,-20) -> (30,-23)  arc c=(30,-20)  first lap: the corner as one arc
  ... the whole ring ...
 12 Feed (33,20) -> (33,0)
 13 Feed (33,0) -> (33,-20)                   overlap toward the exit
 14-27 Feed (33,-20) -> ... -> (30,-23)       the same corner again, as 14 straight chords
 28 Feed (30,-23) -> (0,-23)                  to the exit point's projection
 29 Feed (0,-23) -> (-8,-23)                  lead-out
```

The chords of moves 14–27 lie inside move 5's arc, and the crossing law reads each as crossing it at the same depth.

## Neighbour cases that work (same document)

| Contour | `verify` | Post |
|---|---|---|
| no start or exit point | clean | 67 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0] only | clean | 67 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0], `exit_point` [30, −10] (overlap stays on the straight right wall) | clean | 69 lines |
| `start_point` [30, 0], `exit_point` [0, −20] (overlap passes the corner arc) | 18 crossings | refused |

## Root cause (likely)

`crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_start.rs` says it for #1473: "the ring is cut all the way round, then on along its own polyline to the pick's projection". The first lap reaches the post arc-fitted (move 5 is one arc). The overlap is the ring's raw polyline (the 14 chords). Verify law (a) (`crossing`) then sees chord against arc at shared depth.

An overlap on straight segments only, which repeats exact segments, is not flagged. This is read from the moves above; the fitting call was not traced.

## Expected

The overlap to an exit point re-cuts the ring along the same moves the first lap used (the same arcs), so the program verifies and posts like the start-point-only contour. The overlap must not be refused for re-tracing its own wall.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal program refused. Putting the exit on the start's own edge works around it.
- `effort:high`
- `area:2d`
- `source:agent`

Related: #1473 (start and exit points), #1448.

## Problem

PR #2192 (#2181) calculates the stock removal before playback. During the calculation the playback worker serves no frame. On the dense face fixture the calculation takes 23.9 s in release. During that time the sheet stands and only the progress line changes.

## Proposal

Serve the requested playback frames while the calculation runs. One option: a second field cuts to the playhead while the first field makes the keyframes. Another option: the calculation pauses at each request, serves the frame, and continues.

title: useRadiusArcs posts helix half-turns whose R cannot reach the end point (chord 2.469 > 2R 2.468): R and end points are rounded separately, near-180 arcs are not split

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

With the script option `useRadiusArcs: true` (#258), the Fanuc post writes the helix entry's half-turns as R arcs that no circle of the written radius can draw. The chord between the posted end points is longer than 2R:

```
G03 X2.501 Y-0.493 Z11. R1.235 F1200
G03 X0.032 Y-0.493 Z10. R1.234 F1200      <- from (2.501, -0.493): chord 2.469, 2R = 2.468
```

The two half-turns of one helix also get two different radii, R1.235 and R1.234.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate with a Ø25, 5 mm deep round pocket: a closed, outward-wound ASCII STL with 96-segment walls. The pocket floor face is picked; Bottom Z is `bottom_of_selection`. The document's post is the default Fanuc. Post without a `post` name, because #2190 drops script options when one is named.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "round.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "PW", "source": "round", "params": {"strategy": "waterline", "stepdown": 5}}],
 ["set_operation_geometry", {"operation": "PW", "picks": [{"model": "round", "id": "<pocket floor face>"}]}],
 ["edit_operation", {"name": "PW", "params": {"bottom_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "bottom_of_selection"}, "helix_radius": 1.2344}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "PW"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"script_options": {"useRadiusArcs": true}}],
 ["post", {"output": "r.nc"}]]
```

`verify` is clean and the post succeeds. Four of the helix half-turns have chord − 2|R| = +0.001 mm: arcs whose end point the radius cannot reach.

## Neighbour case that works

The same job with the seeded `helix_radius` of 1.2 (0.4 × the 6 mm tool's radius) posts R1.2 half-turns whose chord is exactly 2.400 = 2R. Across its 32 arcs, none has a chord over 2|R| and none sweeps more than 180°. With `useRadiusArcs` off, the 1.2344 helix posts as I/J.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`emitArcWithRadius` in `assets/posts/fanuc.cps` writes `R` as the unrounded distance from the start point to the centre. It writes X/Y as the end point, each rounded separately to three decimals. It splits only an exact full circle (`< 1e-5`). An arc at or near 180°, which every helix half-turn is, keeps a chord equal to 2R before rounding. Rounding the end points and R separately can then put the chord over 2R, as above.

The same function, with the same full-circle-only split, is in `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `tormach.cps` and `grblhal.cps` (they were not run here).

## Expected

R-form output never posts an arc whose R cannot reach its end point. For example, arcs at or near 180° stay in I/J or are split, as the exact full circle already is. The written R and end points then agree after rounding.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1`: wrong posted G-code, but only with `useRadiusArcs` on (off by default).
- `effort:high`
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

body:
## What happens

Per-post script options stored with `set_post_options { "script_options": ... }` (#258) are dropped without a word when the MCP `post` tool is given a `post` name. That includes naming the post the document already uses. The same document posted without a `post` name applies them.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["generate", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"script_options": {"showSequenceNumbers": "every-block", "writeToolList": true, "safeRetract": "G53"}}],
 ["post", {"output": "named.nc", "post": "Fanuc"}],
 ["post", {"output": "doc.nc"}]]
```

`set_post_options` answers with `"post": "Fanuc (built-in)"` and the three options set. Both posts succeed with no warning.

`doc.nc` (no `post` named) has them:

```
O0001 (VMC 3-AXIS)
(T1 - FLAT END MILL D10. EM-1000-4FL)
N10 G21
...
N340 G53 G00 Z0.
N350 M30
```

`named.nc` (`"post": "Fanuc"`) has none of them: no N words, no tool list, and the default `G28` retract instead of the chosen `G53`.

The same happens with `useRadiusArcs: true` on a round waterline pocket. `"post": "Fanuc"` writes every arc with I/J, byte-identical to the option off.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`posting::program_options_for_script` merges the stored options only when it is given the post:

```rust
let mut overrides = post
    .map(|p| crate::setup_post_options::script_for_post(world, setup, p))
    .unwrap_or_default();
```

The MCP `post` tool calls `script::api::v_post`. With a `cps` given, that goes through `posting_mounts::post_mounts_script_with_options` → `posting::post_script_with_script_options`, which calls `post_script_as(..., None, None, extra)`. With `post: None` the stored options are never read. Only `extra` would apply: `v_post`'s `options` key, which the MCP `post` tool does not expose.

## Expected

When the named post is one the stored options belong to (here, the document's own Fanuc), those options apply, as they do with no name given. Otherwise the post says it did not apply them; it must not drop the user's `safeRetract` or arc form unseen.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a set option that silently does nothing on one path.
- `effort:medium`
- `area:post`
- `area:mcp`
- `source:agent`

Seven of the ten built-in and shipped mill posts ignore it without a word.

The program still ends in its own unit, so the control is left in the unit the user asked to leave behind. #596's reason for the option ("a mm program on an inch-run control leaves the DRO and MDI in mm") is unmet, and nothing tells the user.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],

```

`set_post_options` accepts the value, and both posts succeed with no warning. `diff before.nc after.nc`:

| Post | Change |
|---|---|

The older Post page gates its own "End in" picker to the Tormach PathPilot post (`post_options::end_units_picker`). The new dialog and the MCP tool do not gate it.

#757 settled the same shape for Smoothing: a post that cannot write the asked smoothing says so once ("SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN") instead of dropping it silently.

Each post either writes the asked end unit (`G20` / `G21`, or the control's own word) before the end of the program, or says once that it did not. A choice the post ignores is not offered as if it worked.

title: MCP post with per_op on writes one combined program whose setup change has no stop or home: S2's operations run straight after S1's

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

With the post option `per_op` ("Write one standalone program file per operation") on, the MCP `post` tool writes **one combined program**, and the setup change inside it has no stop and no home move. Setup S2's first operation follows S1's last operation directly:

```
G00 X33. Y17. Z35.
M9
M5
(SETUP: S2)
(OPERATION: F3 - FACE - G54)
G90 G54 G40 G49 G80
(T02 EM-1000-4FL - FLAT END MILL D10)
T02 M6
```

On a machine, S2's toolpath then runs on the part still mounted for S1.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}],
 ["add_setup", {"name": "S1"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}], ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "F2"}],
 ["add_setup", {"name": "S2", "datum_from": "S1"}],
 ["activate_setup", {"name": "S2"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F3"}],
 ["generate", {}], ["verify", {}],
 ["set_post_options", {"per_op": true}],
 ["post", {"output": "perop.nc", "post": "Fanuc"}]]
```

`verify` is clean. `post` returns one file, `perop.nc`, 115 lines, with the excerpt above at the S1 → S2 change.

## Neighbour cases

Same document, same `post` call, only the option differs:

| Option | Output at the S1 → S2 change |
|---|---|
| default (`between_setups: "pause"`) | 119 lines: `G91 G28 Z0` / `G90` / `(SETUP CHANGE - NEXT: S2)` / `M0` |
| `between_setups: "optional-stop"` | the same with `M1` |
| `between_setups: "file-per-setup"` | two files, `..._01_S1.nc` (80 lines) and `..._02_S2.nc` (42 lines) |
| `between_setups: "continue"` | no stop: the user's explicit choice |
| `per_op: true` | no stop, and one combined file |

In the GUI, Output "One file per operation" writes "each operation as its own standalone program into a folder" (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`, #111). The browser build refuses that post outright (`browser_files::refusal`, `NO_FOLDER`). Neither GUI path writes this combined program.

## Root cause (confirmed)

- `stop_of` in `crates/app/src/posting_setup_change.rs` returns no stop whenever `per_op` is set ("run straight on, one file per setup, or one file per operation"). The stop is dropped in the stream, before any post script runs, so every post is affected.
- The MCP `post` tool calls the script API's `v_post` (`crates/app/src/script/api.rs`). That writes through `posting::post_mounts_script_with_options` / `post_mounts_with_script_options`: one program per mount, and never `post_per_op`.

So `per_op` removes the stop that only per-operation files make safe, and this path then writes the operations into one file anyway. The same holds for a script's `cam.post`.

## Expected

The MCP `post` (and `cam.post`) with `per_op` on writes one file per operation, as the GUI does, or refuses by name. It must never write a combined program whose setup change has lost its stop.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1`: wrong posted G-code; a setup change runs on without the operator's stop.
- `effort:high`
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3

body:
## What happens

On a model whose shell `pick::align::outward_normal` cannot judge, `list_features` still prints a definite `facing` and `normal` for each face. These are the sign-canonical plane normal, so a bottom face reads `"facing": "up"`. Opposite walls share one normal. Nothing in the row says the outside was not known.

`lay_part_on_face` on the same face refuses, naming the reason:

```
list_features:    face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3  "facing": "up", "normal": [0.0, 0.0, 1.0]   bounds z 0.0 .. 0.0  (the bottom)
lay_part_on_face: face 0x38c06ba55fa364b3 of 'plate' belongs to an open body (its shell has holes), so its outside cannot be told - repair the mesh (fill its holes) or align to a closed part
```

This is the case #884 and #956 named: an agent picks faces by `facing` and `normal` for `locate_part`, `set_wcs_from_features` and operation geometry.

## Reproduction (main 4b7a6b1e, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

The part is a 60 × 40 × 10 plate (z 0 to 10) with a 30 × 20 pocket, 5 deep, written as ASCII STL with outward winding (28 facets). Its top face is written as four rectangles around the pocket opening, so their long edges meet the pocket's top edges in T-junctions. Every facet is wound outward. For example, the bottom face's facets have normal −Z.

```json
[["import_model", {"path": "plate.stl"}],
 ["list_features", {"model": "plate"}],
 ["add_setup", {}],
 ["lay_part_on_face", {"face": {"model": "plate", "id": "face:0x38c06ba55fa364b3"}}]]
```

`list_features` faces, as printed:

| Face (bounds) | `facing` | `normal` |
|---|---|---|
| bottom, z 0 | `up` | `[0, 0, 1]` |
| wall y = −20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall y = +20 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| wall x = −30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| wall x = +30 | `side` | `[1, 0, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = −10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |
| pocket wall y = +10 | `side` | `[0, 1, 0]` |

`lay_part_on_face` refuses as quoted above.

## Neighbour case that works

The same plate with its top ring written as four trapezoids, so every edge is shared by exactly two facets, is a closed shell. `list_features` gives the bottom `"down"` `[0, 0, -1]`, the walls their outward normals (`[0, -1, 0]` / `[0, 1, 0]`, `[-1, 0, 0]` / `[1, 0, 0]`), and the pocket walls pointing into the pocket. `lay_part_on_face` on its bottom succeeds ("Flip over X", outside −Z).

## Root cause (confirmed)

`outward()` in `crates/app/src/mcp/features.rs` calls `outward_normal` and, when it refuses, falls back to `world_dir(loc, fa.normal)`, the canonical normal. Its comment: "Where it refuses (an open or inside-out shell, no usable plane) the row keeps the canonical normal, placed - a listing must not fail on one face". `facing()` then makes "up" / "down" / "side" from whichever normal it got.

#956's "Done means" asked for the outward normal "or a refusal-shaped field when the winding is not decidable". The shipped fix (PR #1046) took the first half only.

The `camcraft-mcp` skill still carries #937's caveat in the `set_wcs_from_features` row: "a `list_features` face row's `normal` is the plane's canonical normal, not its outward side - tell faces apart by `bounds`". #956 asked for that note to be removed. As it stands, it is wrong for closed shells and is the only warning for open ones.

## Expected

The listing must not fail on one face, and it must not guess either. A face whose outside cannot be told says so in its row: for example, `facing` and `normal` null, or a flag with `outward_normal`'s reason. The skill note then describes that field instead of the old caveat.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a misleading field on the agent surface. The tools that act on a face refuse correctly.
- `effort:medium`: one module plus the skill row.
- `area:mcp`
- `source:agent`

body:
Asked for by the maintainer in chat on 2026-11-16:

> issue enhancement; all the "voxel animation" should not be realtime, it should be pre-calculation so it doesnt lag behind while playing the simulation.

What happens now:

- The simulation calculates the stock removal while the playback runs.
- On a long or dense toolpath the stock picture comes later than the tool position. The animation lags.

What is wanted:

- The stock removal is calculated before the playback, not during it.
- During playback the stock picture is at the tool position at each moment, at each playback speed, and when the user moves the time slider forward or back.

Points for the design (record the choices in `docs/decisions/`):

- Where the calculation runs: a background job after generation, or at the first press of Play, with a progress display and a cancel control. The UI must not stop during it.
- What is stored: stock states at fixed steps of the program (keyframes) plus a fast replay between them, or a full list of states. Give the memory limit and what happens when a job exceeds it.
- When the stored result becomes invalid: an edit of the operation, the tool, the stock, the fixture or the setup. Use the same stamp that the operation cache uses, so that an old stock picture is never shown for a new toolpath.
- The result is ephemeral UI state. It does not go into the project file and it is not a command.
- All resources of an operation are freed when the operation is deleted (AGENTS.md, delete hooks).
- The verify step and the checks that can block the post do not change. This work changes the display only. The PR pins that.

title: Tool body: a holder band that only touches the shank top widens the judged shank

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found during #2176 (PR #2179).

## What happens

`HolderProfile::enclose` (`crates/tools/src/holder_profile.rs`) sets the judged `shank_d` from `reach_over(flute_len, shank_top)`. `reach_over` uses inclusive bounds (`b.above <= hi && b.above + b.len >= lo`). Thus a holder band that starts exactly at the shank top widens the full judged shank to the band radius.

Example: the catalog tool `EM-0400-2FL` (Ø12 shank) with a drawn cone holder from r 10 to r 30 at the shank top. The judged `shank_d` is 60 mm. The shank laws then sweep a Ø60 shank from the flute top to the holder foot.

## Why it matters

The result is conservative, so it is not a gouge. But it can refuse a legal program: a shank law can report a collision that the real Ø12 shank does not make.

## Open questions

- Must the bound be exclusive at the shank top, or must only the band part below the shank top count?
- Which tests pin the current widening on purpose (#368, #828)?

Done means: a test pins that a band that only touches the shank top does not widen the judged shank, and no collision law reads a smaller body than the real one.

This is under the safety floor (a collision check), so it is `effort:high`.

Add the `NestDef` document entity, `.camproj` persistence, cut-data preset lookup, undoable nest commands, and per-sheet setup generation in `camcraft-app`.

Depends on #2158, #2159, and #1862.

## Scope

- **Schema and `.camproj` persistence (`crates/app/src/schema.rs`, `crates/app/src/project/`):**
  - Add `NestDef` in `crates/app/src/schema.rs` and register it in `register_schema`.
  - Store sheet dimensions (`width`, `height`, `thickness`), `edge_margin`, `cut_width` (kerf or router tool diameter), `part_gap`, `allow_parts_in_holes`, material/thickness preset key, part entries (referencing `Sketch` or 3D model silhouettes by name, quantity, optional `sheet_face`, rotation mode, `allow_mirror`, default cut side, per-`ChainId` overrides), and the deterministic solved `NestLayout`.
  - Store placed instance transforms (`tx`, `ty`, `angle_deg`, `mirrored`) and sheet metrics (`utilization_pct`, `sheet_count`, per-sheet `placed_counts`, `unplaced`) without duplicating source geometry.
  - Add `EntityKind::Nest` and `NestDto` in `crates/app/src/project/`, and bump `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- **Material preset lookup (`#1521`, `#1881`, `#1886`):**
  - Read material type, thickness, kerf, cut feed, and pierce dwell from the mounted machine or tool cut-data presets (`crates/tools/src/cutting_rows.rs` / `#1886`).
  - Do not keep a duplicate hardcoded material table in the nest module.
  - Allow explicit user overrides for sheet thickness, cut width, and feed when no preset matches.
- **Undoable commands (`crates/app/src/commands/`):**
  - Implement `CreateNest`, `EditNest`, `AddNestPart`, `RemoveNestPart`, `SetNestProfileSide`, `RunNesting`, and `DeleteNest`.
  - Validate every parameter, quantity, cut width, and rotation step at command construction (never inside systems).
  - Have `RunNesting` compute the deterministic layout from `#2158` and `#2159`, store it in `NestDef`, and create or update one `Setup` per sheet with `StockShape::Box` (`width x height x thickness`).
  - Ensure `undo` and `redo` restore both `NestDef` and any created sheet setups cleanly.

## Done means

Tests in `crates/app` create a nest from multiple `Sketch` and model parts with quantities and cut sides, look up material/thickness/kerf presets from cut data, run deterministic multi-sheet nesting into sheet setups with `StockShape::Box`, report per-sheet counts per part, round-trip `.camproj` and `undo`/`redo`, and refuse invalid numbers or oversized unplaced parts by name.

Part of #2156

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Add a deterministic 2D true-shape nesting kernel in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/` (no ECS, no world).

## Sources and clean room

Write this module from published literature and CamCraft code only:
- Bennell and Oliveira, *The geometry of nesting problems: a tutorial*, EJOR 2008.
- Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell, *A new bottom-left-fill heuristic algorithm for the two-dimensional irregular packing problem*, Operations Research 2006.
- Burke, Hellier, Kendall, and Whitwell, *Complete and robust no-fit polygon generation for the irregular stock cutting problem*, EJOR 2007.
- Reuse `crates/geometry/src/geo2d.rs` (`Region`, `Loop`, `Point2`, `Region::offset_sharp`) and `crates/geometry/src/geo2d/sweep.rs` (`Region::sweep`).
- Do not read or adapt code from HSMWorks, Autodesk Fusion, WAM, SVGnest, or Deepnest.

## Scope

- Define clean input and output structs in `crates/geometry/src/nesting/`:
  - Sheet input: width, height, `edge_margin`, `cut_width` (kerf or router cutter diameter), `part_gap`, and `allow_parts_in_holes`.
  - Part input: stable part id, quantity, outer loop, hole loops, optional open chains, default cut side (`Outside`, `OnLine`, `Inside`), `rotation_mode` (`Locked`, `Orthogonal`, `FixedStep(deg)`), and `allow_mirror`.
- Inflate each part before nesting so separate cuts keep at least `part_gap` of uncut material between cut edges:
  - Inflate `Outside` outer loops by `cut_width + part_gap / 2`.
  - Inflate `OnLine` outer loops by `cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2`.
  - Inflate `Inside` outer loops by `part_gap / 2`.
  - Buffer standalone open chains via `Region::sweep` (`cut_width / 2 + part_gap / 2` for `OnLine`, `cut_width + part_gap / 2` for side cuts).
  - Support router single-slot clearance mode (`part_gap >= cut_width`) when adjacent outside profiles share a single cutter-width channel.
- Shrink the usable sheet inward by `edge_margin` (plus outer `cut_width` clearance) via `Region::offset_sharp`.
- Compute No-Fit Polygons (NFP) and Inner-Fit Polygons (IFP) on the `geo2d::SCALE` (1-micron) grid.
- Place parts with deterministic Bottom-Left-Fill (BLF):
  - Sort parts by decreasing area first. Break ties by part id and instance index.
  - Try candidate rotations (and mirroring only when `allow_mirror` is true).
  - Place small parts inside usable closed holes (`IFP(hole_usable, part_inflated)`) when `allow_parts_in_holes` is true.
  - Open new sheets when parts do not fit on active sheets.
- Report `sheet_count`, per-sheet placed counts per part (`placed_counts`), total placed vs requested quantities, per-sheet and overall `utilization_pct` (`sum(part_net_area) / sheet_area * 100.0`), `waste_region` (`sheet_region.difference(&union_of_cut_footprints)`), used sheet bounds, and an explicit `unplaced` list with refusal reasons.
- Add the one-line provenance comment at the module head.

## Done means

Unit tests in `crates/geometry` nest irregular parts, parts with holes, and swept open chains deterministically across 1 and multiple sheets, report exact per-sheet part counts and `utilization_pct`, place a small part inside a large part hole with full clearance, confirm zero overlap among inflated footprints, verify waste `Region`, and refuse non-finite, negative, or oversized inputs by name.

Part of #2156

title: The post trusts a cached verdict made under the old rapids law

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
What happens: PR #2138 changed the rapid law: a lateral rapid at or above the clearance plane is now re-read against the program ahead, and a traverse through stock under the stock top is convicted (Warning::RapidInStock). A project saved before that change carries cached verdicts made under the old law. The post gate counts only the WARN records that ride the stream from the cache. It does not re-run the rapid law. The stamp digest did not change, so an old cache still reads fresh. The user opens the project, posts without generating, and gets G-code that traverses rapids through uncut stock with no warning.

Expected: a change to a verdict law marks cached verdicts stale. Two known mechanisms: a project-version migration (the v29 -> v30 line in project/apply.rs did exactly this for the sweep_hit alphabet: "a cached verdict from the old laws re-derives stale"), or a salt bump of the op stamp (stamp.rs writes b"camcraft-op-stamp-v2").

Evidence: posting.rs line 501: "Cached generation warnings ride the stream as WARN records, so the engine's own warning count is the gate." The gate in program_ops checks tool, spindle law, and OpStatus only. No path at post time re-runs verify::rapids (grep over posting.rs, posting_per_op.rs, program_entry.rs: no verify call). e7050be17 (the fix of #2121) touches neither project/ nor the stamp salt.

Found while reviewing #2138 (lane review comment 6911362655, non-blocking note).

Done means: one mechanism is chosen and shipped; a test posts a document whose cache holds a pre-law "clear" verdict for a traverse-through-stock path, and the post refuses with a named regenerate instruction.

title: Tilted plane (3+2): a Tool axis A of 180 degrees is refused with no reason, and the plane of the A0 B180 face has X and Y exchanged

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found during the work on #1904 ("Your first 4-axis part", Tormach 770MX + microARC 4), on `main` at `af83da0f4`.

A 4th-axis table about X can turn the part to A180. `tormach.cps` posts that index as `G0 A180`, and `the_canonical_b180_pose_posts_as_a180` pins it. But the operation page does not let the user ask for it directly.

## 1. A Tool axis A of 180 is refused, and the refusal gives no reason

Steps:
1. Mount `Tormach 770MX + microARC 4`. Add a tool and a box stock.
2. Add a Slot. On the Heights tab, tick **Tilted plane (3+2)**. Set **Tool axis A** to 180 and **Tool axis B** to 0. Choose **Apply**.

Result: the edit is refused with this text: `operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`. The MCP tool gives the same text: `add_operation: invalid parameters: operation parameters are not usable for a Slot operation`.

The cause is `Tilt::is_sane` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`. It accepts A from -90 to 90 and B from -180 to 180. The pose law writes the face opposite the top as A 0, B 180. The refusal does not name the tilt, the limits, or the A 0 B 180 pose. A microARC 4 user thinks in A only, and cannot find the remedy from this text.

The workaround is to type A 0 and B 180. The guide page for #1904 documents it.

## 2. The plane of the A 0 B 180 face has X and Y exchanged

`TiltedFrame::new` (`crates/cl/src/cl/frame.rs`) selects the in-plane axes from the smallest component of the tool axis. For A 90 and A -90, plane X is machine X (the rotary axis). For A 0 B 180, `sin(180 degrees)` is not exactly zero, the seed becomes Y, and plane X is machine Y and plane Y is machine X.

Result: the same flat along the bar has the ends (-0.75, 0) and (-0.25, 0) on three faces, but (0, -0.75) and (0, -0.25) on the fourth face. The page does not show the plane axes, so the user finds this only from the toolpath preview.

The posted program is correct in each case. The post reads the tool tip in machine coordinates.

## Proposed change

- Refuse an out-of-range tilt by name. Give the limits, and say that the face opposite the top is A 0 B 180.
- Or accept A beyond 90 degrees at the door and store the canonical pose.
- For a pose with no X component of the tool axis, keep plane X on machine X. Or show the plane X and Y directions on the page.

A change to the frame basis changes the paths of existing A 0 B 180 operations. Thus this work is under the safety floor.

Done means: a user who types Tool axis A = 180 on an A-table machine gets the A180 index or a refusal that names the remedy. The plane X of the A 0 B 180 face is on the rotary axis, or the page shows the plane axes. A test pins each item. The guide page `first-4axis-part.md` is updated.

Refs #1904, #797.

body:
The user wants Sodick wire EDM support, including 4-axis (taper / U V) cuts.

Today the Sodick post refuses 4-axis cuts by name, on purpose (#1497, PR #2120, decision `docs/decisions/1497-sodick-four-axis.md`). In the 1998 Sodick manual, U V are offsets from X Y; X Y sit on the part's bottom plane; and the program planes are measured from the worktable. CamCraft's machine file and toolpath stream state the wire guide planes, but not the worktable heights, so the guide-plane values cannot be converted to Sodick's planes. Writing them unconverted would post a wrong 4-axis cut.

What is needed:
- Machine-file keys for the Sodick plane heights the manual uses (worktable to lower guide, worktable to program plane / part bottom, upper guide), with sources; refusal by name when a taper cut needs them and they are missing.
- The conversion from CamCraft's guide planes to Sodick's planes, from the published manual only (clean-room).
- G74/G75 output and U V words, with goldens; an air-cut test kit for an owner of a Sodick (the Discord user who has one).

Done means: a machine file that states the heights posts a 4-axis taper cut whose U V and plane words match the manual's worked example; without the heights, the cut is refused by name; existing 2-axis output is byte-identical.

Refs #1497, #617.

title: Rapid law skips rapids AT the clearance plane: a clearance set inside the stock rapids through uncut stock and posts with no warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while working #1559 (issue-worker-high, upstream main ce59ef446).

## What happens

The rapid law convicts "rapid move N travels below the clearance plane inside stock" - a rapid **at** the clearance plane is never judged. So when the clearance plane itself is set inside the stock (a Fixed height, or Top-of-Model + an offset smaller than the stock allowance), the op's traverse runs through uncut stock and the program **posts with no warning**.

Reproduced headlessly (synthetic fixture of `crates/app/tests/top_stock.rs`):

- Stock box 40 x 40 x 10 (top Z10), part a 10 x 10 x 5 cube at the origin.
- 2D Contour on the part, `clearance_z = Fixed 8`, `retract_z = Fixed 8`, Top 5, Bottom 0, stepdown 2.5, Plunge entry.
- Generated path: move 0 `Rapid (0,0,8) -> (10.35,-2.98,8)` - a lateral rapid 2 mm under the stock top, through the stock; the machine also arrives at Z8 over (0,0), inside the stock column.
- `tp.warnings == []`, and `posting::post_setup_unwritten` returns `Ok`.

Nothing at command creation refuses a clearance below the stock top either (Contour validation only checks clearance >= Top, retract >= Top).

## Why P1

A rapid through uncut stock is a collision that passes (AGENTS.md P1: "a gouge or collision that passes"). The default heights reference the stock top, so a user has to set the plane low, but a Fixed or model-referenced clearance on a taller stock is ordinary input.

## Done means

- A rapid at (not only under) the clearance plane that passes through stock the program ahead has not removed is convicted (`RapidInStock` or a named clearance-in-stock warning) and holds the post - or a clearance/retract plane under the remaining stock top over the op's travel is refused by name at generation.
- Pinned by a test for the repro above (Contour) and one other ladder kind; the #96/#1066/#1091 rapid-law pins unchanged.

Related: #1559 (entry over carried stock), #96, #104, #1095.

body:
Part of #1490. Found while working #2031 (the motion-crate generator `camcraft_motion::machining2d::rest_adaptive`).

What happens: the rest Adaptive plan is correct and holds the load, but it travels a lot out of cut. Measured (debug build, 4 mm tool after a 12 mm tool, two depths; cut / air feed / rapid in mm):

| Fixture | Passes a depth | Plunges a depth | Cut | Air feed | Rapid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners | 40 | 4 | 224 | 967 | 360 |
| 70 x 50 with a 14 x 14 island | 36 | 4 | 250 | 955 | 450 |
| two 30 x 30 bays, 10 mm neck | 128 | 37 | 954 | 3445 | 1337 |

Why: the verifier's crossing law reads exact signs, so a pass that rides a wall retraces the area's first way in and first way out on the wall's own vertices, and returns on one chord (`adaptive/rest/leads.rs`, `canon.rs`). Every pass of a corner pays that wall ride and the return. In a neck, a half loop whose return would cross an earlier feed is reached by a retract instead. The plain Adaptive holds its plans to 1.5 times the cut length out of cut and 8 retract hops a level (`pocket_hsm::over_budget`); rest Adaptive is not held to that yet. The posted path is chords only (no arc fit): 3216 moves for the corner fixture, 14850 for the neck.

Ideas, none tried: shorten the retrace to the previous pass's landing instead of the area's first; lifted returns as the plain Adaptive's (`adaptive/lift.rs`); arcs fitted and proved inside the center area (`arc_proof.rs`) with the load re-read on the fitted path.

Done means: rest Adaptive is held to a stated out-of-cut and retract budget (the plain Adaptive's, or a recorded one of its own) with a named refusal or fallback past it; the readings above are re-measured and recorded; every law of `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/` still holds.

title: camcraft-ui: --help does not list the MCP, GPU and other start options

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-16. His words: "there is flags on camcraft-ui app, but "--help" wont show the options for mcp and it settings for example or overriding gpu and such"

## What happens

The `camcraft-ui` program reads start options, but `--help` does not show them. The user cannot find them without the source.

The options that the source reads (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/mod.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/gpu.rs`, `crates/ui/src/lib.rs`):

- `--gpu-backend <name>` and the variable `CAMCRAFT_GPU_BACKEND`
- `--gpu <adapter name>` and the variable `CAMCRAFT_GPU`
- the MCP port option and the variable `CAMCRAFT_MCP_PORT`
- `--headless`
- `--ui`

The worker must find each option and each variable that the program reads. This list can be incomplete.

## Expected

`camcraft-ui --help` prints each start option and each environment variable, with its value form, its default and one line that says what it does. It then exits with code 0 and opens no window.

## What to do

1. Keep the options in one table (name, value form, environment variable, default, help line). The parser and the help text read the same table, so that they cannot disagree.
2. `--help` and `-h` print the help text and exit before a window or a GPU device is made.
3. `--version` prints the version and exits.
4. An option that the program does not know gives a clean error that names it and points to `--help`. The program does not start with a wrong option ignored.
5. Write the help text in plain English (no G-code terms).
6. Add the options to the user guide page that describes how to start the program.

## Done means

- A test asserts that the help text names each option of the table and each environment variable.
- A test asserts that each flag string that the parser reads is in the table.
- A test asserts that an unknown option gives the error and no window.
- The PR body has the printed `--help` text.
