body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-16. His words: "its just to much compile in each "batch".. so it takes forever to get thru a post-merge-gate - even with -j6 set.. if u set a -j6.. there should be 2 cores per procss. so a max of 3 tests per batch.."

## What happens

- `xtask/src/plan.rs` gives each cargo step `-j 6` and `--test-threads=6` (`J`, `T`).
- `xtask/src/lanes.rs` runs up to `LIMIT = 4` steps at the same time in the release tier.
- Each lane keeps the full `-j 6` and `--test-threads=6`. Four lanes thus start up to 24 compile jobs and 24 test threads.
- The gate also shares its machine with review builds and worker builds. Each of those uses `-j 6` too.
- The result is more jobs than cores. Each lane is slower than a serial run.

## What to do

1. Make the job count one budget for the whole gate (default 6). Read it from one constant, with an environment override.
2. When N lanes run at the same time, give each lane `-j (budget / N)` and `--test-threads=(budget / N)`, minimum 1.
3. Set the lane limit from the budget: at most `budget / 2` lanes. With a budget of 6 this is 3 lanes with 2 jobs each.
4. A step that runs alone keeps the full budget.
5. Print the budget, the lane count and the jobs for each lane at the start of the gate.
6. Apply the same rule to each tier that runs lanes, and to #1941 if it adds lanes to the quick and batch tiers.
7. Update the `gate` skill and the `runners` skill: the sum of `-j` of all builds on one machine stays at or below its core count.

## Done means

- A unit test in `xtask` shows that the sum of `-j` in each wave is at or below the budget, and that no wave has more than `budget / 2` lanes.
- A unit test shows that a step that runs alone gets the full budget.
- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run` prints the budget and the jobs for each lane.
- The PR body has the wall time of one batch run and one release wave, before and after.
- The PR body has the line `Process change: yes`.

**What is wanted**

- If a new app command is necessary, it gets its MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"). The MCP `move_model` tool already sets the rotation.
- Pin the behaviour in structural and interaction tests, not in PNG snapshots.

Depends on PR #1330 (the Move mode and the `move_drag` module). Stack on that PR, or start after it merges.

title: 2D rest Adaptive: plan engagement from proved remaining stock

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Part of #1490.

The 2D rest generator refuses Adaptive by name. The current adaptive planner starts with a full pocket and its own entry bore.

Implement Adaptive over the material that earlier operations leave. Keep the existing refusal until the required stock and entry proofs are available.

Design decision:
- Give the planner a separate legal cutter-center region and conservative remaining-material region at each cut depth.
- Derive cleared space from verified previous-operation stock. Do not treat an entered previous diameter as proof that material is absent.
- Initialize engagement from remaining material. Do not initialize it from the whole pocket or assume that the entry bore exists.
- Prove the whole cutter footprint and approach volume clear before using a cleared-space entry or rapid.
- Refuse uncertain stock, missing cut depth, and an entry with no proved clearance by name.
- Preserve the conservative remaining-material bound when rasterizing. Uncertain cells contain material.
- Keep the bounded planner work budget and named refusal when the load or coverage cannot be proved.

Tests:
- Use a rounded pocket with four corner residues after a larger tool.
- Measure engagement against simulated previous cuts at every requested depth.
- Cover islands, disconnected rest areas, narrow necks, and a roughing pass that stops above the rest floor.
- Prove no rapid meets material, every emitted path passes verification, and reachable rest material is covered.
- Remove each stock, depth, and entry guard separately. Each mutation must fail its pinning test.

Done means: Adaptive runs on proved remaining stock, passes these tests, and refuses unsupported stock or entry cases by name.

Related work: the separate #1490 tasks for carried-stock input and entry from cleared space supply the required proofs. This task adds the adaptive engagement plan.

Literature: M. Held, On the Computational Geometry of Pocket Machining, LNCS 500 (1991), https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/3-540-54103-9. Z. Yao, S. K. Gupta and D. S. Nau, Algorithms for selecting cutters in multi-part milling problems, Computer-Aided Design 35 (2003), https://www.cs.umd.edu/~nau/papers/yao2003algorithms.pdf.

These sources describe pocket geometry and cutter coverage. The clearance and stock-proof contract above is this project's decision. Do not copy another CAM product's code or output.

- `WorkMaterial` (`crates/tools/src/cutting.rs:60-67`) has 6 values and no `Unknown`.
- A tool keeps one `rpm`/`feed` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:209-210`) as the fallback, and `cutting: Vec<CuttingRow>` (L239) with rpm and feed only. There is no stepdown and no stepover in a row.
- `material_group` (L206) is free text.
- The material is one value for the document (`WorkMaterialDef`, `crates/app/src/schema.rs:674-679`; `cutting::material_of`, `crates/app/src/cutting.rs:28`). The setup stock has no material.

## What to do

1. Add `WorkMaterial::Unknown` (word `unknown`). It is the default row of each tool.
2. Add stepdown and stepover to `CuttingRow`. A missing value falls back to the `Unknown` row.
3. Migration: on load, the old `rpm`/`feed` of a tool become its `Unknown` row. `PROJECT_VERSION` 61 to 62 (`crates/app/src/project/file.rs:97`). `.camtools` `VERSION` 1 to 2 (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs:31-33`); the reader accepts 1 and migrates it.
4. Add an optional material to the setup stock. The row is selected by the setup stock material, then the document material, then `Unknown`.
5. Show a table of rows for each material in the Cutting data group of the tool page.
6. Keep the law of `crates/app/src/cutting_rows.rs`: a row moves numbers only inside a command, never on load.

This changes the feeds and speeds that the post reads. It is `effort:high` by the safety floor. An older build refuses the new file: the PR is `feat!` with a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

- A tool has an `Unknown` row, and a new tool gets it.

body:
Found while tracing #2005 on upstream/main cda3d5896. This is a source-trace finding.

The editor preview rebuilds body facets in state_tool_body::tool_body_preview. tool_body_view::preview creates a body with machine_default=false. tool_body_page::envelope returns its raw profile bands.

Collision checks use tool_body::judged. For a machine-default holder, judged calls HolderProfile::floored with the parameter holder. The collision check and sim_tool_body::for_operation therefore retain the conservative parameter-cylinder floor. The editor does not show that floor explicitly. A default holder narrower or shorter than the parameter cylinder can appear smaller than the shape being checked.

Keep the conservative collision rule. Show its effective bands in the editor, or visibly distinguish the draft body from the checked shape. An explicit holder must continue replacing the parameter cylinder.

Done means: a UI test uses a machine-default body smaller than the parameter cylinder and pins the displayed checked envelope; an explicit-body control still replaces the cylinder. No collision or post behavior changes.

Related: #2005.

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0. His words:

> The tool editor page needs a re work, Input fields sitting left of the input, cutting data by material should be default behavior and the default "value" is what we have in the catalog now. We can have a material called "Unknown" that is the default value.  Why there is two previews of the tool is also strange. One drawn profile of the tool and the holder picked should be enough. The holder library, should remove the parametric holder values and "fill them in" with the values from the library.. There is no need for having a Weldon for each "sized tool".. a weldon is a weldon, and whatever tool will fit it.
> In general the Tool editor needs a complete overhaul.

This is an umbrella issue. Research it, then file one sub-issue for each part, and close this issue.

## Parts

1. **Layout.** Put each label on the left of its input field, in a property grid (see the Fusion-style dialog rule: collapsible groups, tooltips).
2. **Cutting data by material is the default.** Each tool has cutting data (speed, feed, stepdown, stepover) for each material. The current single set of values becomes the data of a material named `Unknown`. `Unknown` is the default material. Existing tool libraries and project files load with their values moved to `Unknown`, with no loss.
3. **One preview.** The editor shows one drawing: the tool profile and the holder that the user selected. Remove the second preview. (See #2005: the body and the spun profile draw over each other.)
4. **Holders come from the holder library.** The user selects a holder from the library. The holder values (diameter, length, gauge length) come from the library entry and are not typed into each tool. Remove the parametric holder fields from the tool.
5. **A holder is not sized to a tool.** One holder entry (for example a Weldon holder) serves each tool whose shank fits it. Do not keep one holder entry for each tool size. The fit check (shank diameter against the holder bore) must give a clear refusal when a tool does not fit.

## Questions for the research

- The tool library and project file format change (parts 2, 4, 5). Give the migration and the version bump. This can be a breaking change.
- How the collision check and the simulation get the holder shape after part 4. They must use the same shape that the preview shows.
- Where cutting data by material connects to the operation: the operation uses the material of the setup stock, or `Unknown` when the stock has no material.
- How this joins #2002 (tool settings in Properties, catalog in its own panel). Decide one layout for the two issues.

## Related

#2002, #2003, #2005, #93, #743, #808, #898

## Done means

Each part has a sub-issue with a priority, an effort label and a "Done means" line. This issue lists them and is closed.

title: Depth-stepping operations cut a first level at Top Z that removes no material

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-15, on v0.21.0, with a screenshot of a 2D Adaptive operation.

His words: "a common issue i see is that the first toolpath is always ontop of the part at TopZ ... even thos stepdown states "full depth" of the cut.. technically it should just be one single toolpath right?" and "find it in all operations.. This is a high effortf, P2 bug.."

## What happens

The operation has Top Z = 13 (stock top + 1), Bottom Z = 0 and Stepdown = 50 mm. It posts two full levels: one at Z 13 and one at Z 0. The level at Top Z cuts no material. It doubles the cycle time of a one-level cut.

## Cause

The shared level law starts its list at Top Z:

```rust
// crates/motion/src/machining2d/levels.rs, cut_levels
let mut z = top;
while z > bottom + tol {
    zs.push(z);      // the first level is `top`
    z -= stepdown;
}
zs.push(bottom);
```

`cut_levels(13, 0, 50)` gives `[13, 0]`. The correct list is `[0]`. With a stepdown of 5 it gives `[13, 8, 3, 0]`. The correct list is `[8, 3, 0]`.

`crates/app/src/operation/area.rs` `ladder_planes` restates the same law, and its unit test pins the wrong list (`ladder_planes(20.0, 0.0, 5.0) == [20, 15, 10, 5, 0]`).

## Callers found (read-only search, not complete)

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/`: `adaptive_troch.rs:158`, `bore.rs:308`, `circular.rs:278` and `:280`, `contour_params.rs:216` (2D Contour), `face.rs:156`, `pocket.rs:277`, `pocket_hsm.rs:49` and `pocket_troch.rs:68` (level counts for the budget), `slots.rs:160` and `:343`, `trochoid_slot.rs:319`
- `crates/motion/src/machining3d/entry.rs:89`, `:123`, `:236`, `:258` (3D Pocket and its rest pass)
- `crates/app/src/operation/area.rs:74`, `:182`, `:233` (`ladder_planes`, the 3D pocket region build)
- `crates/motion/tests/control_comp.rs` (a test helper with the same name)

Not yet read: `crates/motion/src/finishing3d/ladder.rs` `levels`, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_depth.rs` `ladder`, `crates/motion/src/machining3d/ladder.rs`, the turning, drilling (peck), engraving, chamfer, plasma and EDM depth ladders, and each operation with its own loop.

## For the work

1. Audit each operation of each machine type for a level at Top Z (or at the material top) that removes no material. List each in the PR with the result.
2. Fix the shared law so that the first level is `top - stepdown`, and the last level is `bottom` exactly. Use one law: `ladder_planes` in `app` must use the motion law, or match it by a shared test.
3. Check the special cases:
   - Top Z below the stock top (material above Top Z): no level may cut more than one stepdown. Find what each operation means by Top Z, and state it.
   - `circular.rs:278` starts at a previous level (`cut_levels(prev, floor, ...)`): make sure that it does not cut the previous level two times.
   - Face: a single pass at `cut_z` stays one pass.
   - A stepdown of 0 or a span of 0: the current refusal and the one-plane result stay.
   - Rest machining and the 3D Pocket shell levels: the level count and the budget readings change. Restate the budget pins with the reason.
   - The ramp, helix and plunge entries that read `top_z` as the material top (`Motion::top_z`) must stay correct.
4. The size of the last step (the remainder or equal steps) is a separate choice. Keep the current remainder rule, and file a follow-up issue for the choice.

This changes posted G-code for existing projects (one level fewer for each depth-stepping operation). It is under the safety floor.

## Done means

- No operation posts a level at Top Z that removes no material when Top Z is at or above the material top.
- One-level case: Top Z 13, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 50 gives one level at Z 0. Pinned for 2D Adaptive, 2D Pocket, 2D Contour, Slot, Bore, Circular and 3D Pocket.
- Multi-level case: Top Z 20, Bottom Z 0, Stepdown 5 gives `[15, 10, 5, 0]`. Pinned on the shared law and on `ladder_planes`.
- Each changed golden is listed in the PR with the reason. The PR says that posted G-code changes.
- Each verify and gouge pin of the touched operations stays green.

title: Research: Haas 5-axis trunnions (TR160/UMC-500), G254 DWO, G234 TCPC, and G93

labels.name: area:post

labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Design 5-axis kinematics and Haas NGC multi-axis posting for trunnion tables (`TR160`, `TR210`, `TRT100`) and universal machining centers (`UMC-500`).

Public Haas specifications and codebase behavior expose these open problems:
- **Kinematics mismatch in CamCraft:** `crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs:53` (`axis_to_angles`) outputs `[A, B, 0.0]` with `C` always zero, and `crates/app/src/machine/judge.rs:79-105` checks literal rotary letters without inverse kinematics. A `UMC-500` uses `B` (+120° to -35°) plus `C` (360°), which fails when any Y-tilted pose requests `A`. A `TR160`/`TRT100` calls its cradle `A` (±120°) and platter `B` (360°), where platter `B` turns perpendicular to tilted `A` rather than around static Y.
- **NGC 5-axis G-codes and options:** Haas NGC uses `G254`/`G255` (Dynamic Work Offset) for 3+2 indexing and `G234` (Tool Center Point Control, not Fanuc `G43.4`) for simultaneous 4/5-axis cutting. Both `G254` and `G234` are paid options (`haascnc.com`); controls without TCPC require `G93` inverse-time feed (`F = 1 / minutes` per move).
- **Brakes and limits:** 4th-axis (`M10`/`M11`) and 5th-axis (`M12`/`M13`) brakes clamp during indexed cuts and stay released (`M11`/`M13`) during simultaneous motion.

Deliver a design decision in `docs/decisions/` covering:
1. Inverse kinematics or kinematic-chain representation in `cl`/`judge.rs` for `B+C` UMCs and `A+B` trunnions (`TR160`/`TRT100`).
2. Option-gating rules in `.mch` and `haas.cps` for `G254`/`G255` (DWO), `G234` (TCPC), `G93` fallback, and `M10`–`M13` brakes.
3. Concrete implementation sub-issues for machine definitions, IK checks, and `haas.cps` 5-axis output.

Done means: A design decision in `docs/decisions/` defines the kinematic model, option gating, and implementation split for Haas 5-axis support.

body:
Add a clean-room Mach4 milling postprocessor (`assets/posts/mach4.cps`) specced solely from public Mach4 and RS-274/NGC documentation.

### Context
- `assets/posts/` and `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` contain no Mach4 or MachMotion post today.
- Standard Mach4 lacks `G43.4` RTCP, supports `G93` inverse-time feed (`F` on every feed block) and `G94`, limits `G2/G3` arcs to Cartesian planes (`G17/G18/G19`), uses `G43 H..`, `G53`/`G28`/`G30` safe retracts, and `G64` constant velocity mode.
- Depends on machine schema (#1962), AC IK solver (#1965), and `G93` timing (#1966).

### Requirements
- Author `assets/posts/mach4.cps` from public Mach4 Mill GCode Programming documentation only (Clean-Room Protocol). Register it in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting.rs`).
- Leave 3-axis programs in standard `G94` mode with `G2/G3` arcs unchanged.
- Handle 3+2 indexed sections by retracting safely in `G94`, positioning `G0 A.. C..` (with optional unclamp/clamp M-codes), and cutting in `G94` with rotated planar coordinates and arcs.
- Handle simultaneous 5-axis sections by outputting no `G43.4`, linearizing arcs to `G1`, switching to `G93`, emitting pre-compensated `X Y Z A C` and `F` on every `G1` block, and restoring `G94` after the section.
- Respect Mach4 rotary rollover settings (`unwrapped` vs `rollover_360` option) and unwind safely only at retract `Z`.
- Refuse tilted/simultaneous posting by name if the machine lacks required trunnion geometry or states `controller.rtcp = true` unexpectedly without matching setup.

Done means: `mach4.cps` posts valid Mach4 G-code for 3-axis, 3+2 indexed, and simultaneous 5-axis sections in mm and inch, refuses missing trunnion geometry by name, and passes golden conformance tests.

### Context
- `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` computes only `G94` feed caps today.
- Under `G93` in Mach4 and RS-274/NGC, `F = 1 / dt_min` (`min^-1`) applies per block, and every feed block requires an `F` word.
- Today the `.cnc` stream does not state explicitly whether a tilted section is 3+2 indexed (`Tilt` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/params.rs`) or simultaneous 5-axis (`crates/motion/src/multiaxis/mod.rs`).

### Requirements
- Emit explicit section mode parameters distinguishing 3-axis, 3+2 indexed, and simultaneous 5-axis without breaking existing `.cl` or golden inputs.
- Compute per-block `dt_cut = ||tip_1 - tip_0|| / v_prog` in part space, plus `dt_lim` from stated linear and rotary `max_normal_speed` ceilings in `min^-1`.
- Take `dt_min = max(dt_cut, dt_lim)`, handle rotary-only reorientations without division by zero, skip zero-motion duplicate moves, and clamp `F = 1 / dt_min` to safe bounds.
- Keep `G93` `F` independent of `G20` (inch) vs `G21` (mm).

Done means: Simultaneous post segments receive finite `G93` `F` values honoring linear and rotary speed limits in both mm and inch, zero-length moves never fail or divide by zero, 3+2 sections stay distinct from simultaneous sections, and 3-axis streams stay unchanged.

body:
Build one shared pure-Rust inverse kinematics solver for table-table XYZAC machines inside `crates/post` so both the machine checker and posts compute the same coordinates.

### Context
- `crates/post/src/post/mod.rs` writes canonical `[A, B, 0]` angles from `cl::axis_to_angles` (`crates/cl/src/cl/pose.rs`), with no AC trunnion kinematics.
- On a non-RTCP table-table machine, tool length stays parallel to machine `Z`, while `A` and `C` rotate the workpiece around `pivot` and child `offset` vectors.

### Requirements
- Implement forward and inverse kinematics using Rodrigues axis-angle rotation for unit rotary vectors and non-zero `A` pivot and `C`-to-`A` offsets.
- Evaluate both analytical branches (`(+A, C)` and `(-A, C + 180 deg)`) against `A.travel` and `C.travel`, and refuse unreachable moves by name.
- Handle `A` near `0` (pole) by holding the previous modal `C` angle instead of snapping `C` to `0`.
- Minimize weighted angular steps across moves to cross `A = 0` smoothly when travel permits, instead of causing 180-degree `C` flips during cuts.
- Unwrap continuous `C` angles inside a simultaneous section within finite `C` limits, and support re-wrapping only at safe retract boundaries.
- Subdivide linear moves whose angular step exceeds chord tolerance so curved rotary motion keeps tool-tip accuracy.

Done means: Unit tests verify round-trip FK/IK (`<= 0.001 mm` tip error) with non-zero offsets, asymmetric `A` limits, smooth pole crossings, continuous `C` unwrapping, and named refusal for unreachable tool orientations.

What happens now:

title: 2D Contour: Side Auto resolves to Outside on a blind bore rim

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

2D Contour with Side Auto on a picked rim of a BLIND bore resolves to Outside. The Outside ring stands in the part below the mouth. Before #1927 the operation cut only the top plane (in air) and posted with no warning. With the #1927 fix (PR on `issue/1927-contour-outside-hole-refusal`) the operation is refused by name ("set Side to Inside").

Fixture: `testdata/models/Milling-test.step`, the closed rim chain of radius 12.5 at Z 20. Test: `crates/app/tests/area_open.rs`, `a_containment_that_puts_the_tool_in_the_part_is_refused_by_name` (the last assert pins the refusal).

## Cause

`selection_geometry_impl` (`crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs`) resolves Auto by the fill ratio: the area of the ring that is part material, read from the part's XY silhouette. The floor of a blind bore fills the silhouette inside the rim. Thus the fill is near 1 and Auto selects Outside. A through hole has an empty silhouette inside the rim, so Auto selects Inside there.

## Done means

- Auto reads the material that the ring bounds at the ring's own level (or just below it), not the full XY silhouette.
- Auto on a blind bore rim resolves to Inside and cuts the wall from inside.
- The last assert of the test above changes to a clean Inside path.
- Auto on a boss and on an outer wall still resolves to Outside.

## Workaround

Set Side to Inside.

## Scope (OEM manuals only)

4. **Siemens Sinumerik 808D Advanced** (`Grizzly G0934` 5' x 10' 8-pos rotary ATC):

Hold implementation behind the `RichAuto DSP A11` post, machine files, and test-cut kit so real hardware feedback stabilizes our shop-router baseline first.

Add a built-in 3-axis router post for the **RichAuto DSP A11** controller in `assets/posts/richauto.cps`. Register it in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` and pin it in `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`.

## Context

Issue #1907 confirmed that mkinney's friend runs a **RichAuto DSP A11** handheld controller. Common Laguna Swift (`4x4`, `4x8`, `5x10`) and Grizzly CNC routers (`G0894`, `G0931`, `G0895`) also use this controller.

CamCraft's existing posts (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, `fanuc.cps`, `carvera.cps`, `tinyg.cps`) do not run safely on a RichAuto A11:
- `grblhal.cps` emits `G91.1`, `G94`, `G53 G0 Z...`, `T<n> M6`, and canned cycles. RichAuto A11 uses the pendant `AbsCntr` menu switch (`Off` = incremental) instead of `G91.1`, and basic router firmware can reject canned cycles or `G91.1`.
- `fanuc.cps` emits `%`, `O0001`, `T.. M6`, `G43 H..`, `G49`, `G91 G28 Z0`, and `G84` tapping.

## Specification (OEM manuals only)

1. **Units and file format:** default to `mm` (`G21`) to match RichAuto's internal metric math and avoid `G20` scale errors. Write `.nc` ASCII files with parentheses comments `(...)`. Omit `%`, `O` program numbers, and `;` comments.
2. **Preamble and arcs:** write `G21`, `G90`, `G17`, `G40`, and `G80`. Omit `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, and `G49`. Emit incremental `I`/`J`/`K` matching `AbsCntr = Off`. Handle `G54` cleanly (`G54` default or document `Read G54` vs `Ign G54` in post notes; handle or refuse multi-WCS safely).
3. **Spindle and warm-up:** write `S<rpm> M3`. Add a configurable spindle dwell property (`G04 P<ms>`, default `0`) so the post works alongside the pendant `Spindle Delay` setting. Document 8-step `S1`-`S8` VFD wiring in post comments.
4. **Drilling and tool changes:** expand all canned drill cycles (`G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G73`, `G86`, `G89`) to plain `G0`/`G1` moves (using the pattern in `assets/posts/carvera.cps` and `tinyg.cps`). Refuse mid-program tool changes on the initial 3-axis manual slice (or lift Z cleanly and write `M0` with `(CHANGE TOOL T<n>)` rather than bare `T<n> M6`).
5. **Refusals and footer:** refuse `G84` tapping, `G41`/`G42` cutter compensation, and probing. Retract Z to clearance height in work coordinates, stop spindle (`M5`) and coolant (`M9` if active), and end with `M30` (no trailing `%`).

## Rules

- Clean room: use only RichAuto DSP A11 OEM documentation, RS-274 / ISO 6983 standards, and CamCraft repository patterns (`assets/posts/AGENTS.md`). Do not read or copy Autodesk, HSMWorks, or third-party CAM posts.

## Done means

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps` exists and registers in `BUILTINS` in `crates/app/src/posting.rs`.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs` passes for `RichAuto DSP A11` across all mill goldens and refuses `G84`, `G41`/`G42`, and probing by name.
- Posted `.nc` output uses `G21`, incremental `I`/`J`, expanded drilling moves, `(...)` comments, safe Z retract, and `M30` with no `%`, `O` headers, `G91.1`, `G43`, or `G49`.
- Decision entry added under `docs/decisions/`.

title: Turning thread: flank passes end short of the G76 end point that the control runs to

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: P7

body:
Found during #1842.

## What happens

With "Threading: G76 cycle" and a flank infeed, the Fanuc lathe post writes one G76 cycle. Two published manuals show that the control ends every pass at the programmed end point D:

- FANUC Series 0i-F lathe operator's manual B-64604EN-1, section 4.2.7, Fig. 4.2.7 (a).
- Siemens SINUMERIK ISO Turning programming manual A5E52211627B, Fig. 4-25.

The turning kernel (`crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, the pass loop) shifts the start AND the end of each pass by the same flank offset. Thus a shallower pass ends short of D by `(k - depth) * tan(a/2)`. Only the root pass ends at D.

## Effect

The control cuts each shallower pass a little longer than the laid pass that the verdict and the stock simulation see. The extra length is at a smaller depth, inside the groove that the root pass cuts to D. It removes no material beyond the root pass and does not move toward a shoulder. Thus this is not a wrong-output defect. But the simulated passes are not exactly the passes that run.

`crates/app/tests/lathe_post_g76_sources.rs::every_pass_runs_to_the_posted_end_z_inside_the_root_pass` pins the present difference.

## Done means

One of these:

- The kernel lays each flank pass of a G76-postable plan to the same end station, and the pin changes to assert that.
- Or a decision records why the present laid ends stay.

body:
Maintainer request from #1572 ("make an issue of using cadmpeg as file importer then i suppose.. we could open all common cad parts into camcraft that way.").

## Goal
Run `cadmpeg` as an optional external CLI process from `camcraft-app` to convert native CAD files into STEP inside a strict sandbox, then import through the existing STEP pipeline.

## Scope
- Add an optional `cadmpeg_path: Option<String>` field to `ViewPrefs` in `crates/app/src/prefs.rs` (`camcraft-prefs/1`) so existing `prefs.json` files still load cleanly.
- Resolve the executable cleanly on desktop (`cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))`): check `cadmpeg_path` first if set, then search `PATH`. Return `CommandError::Needs` naming `cadmpeg` and the file extension when missing.
- Probe `cadmpeg --version` and enforce minimum version `0.6.12`. Probe `cadmpeg formats --json` to confirm STEP export and codec availability. Report old or unusable binaries via named `CommandError` variants (`CommandError::Needs` / `CommandError::Invalid`).
- Pass file paths directly through `std::process::Command::new` argv with no shell invocation.
- Run conversions inside a unique private directory under `std::env::temp_dir()` owned by an RAII `Drop` guard that removes the directory on success, error, or panic.
- Enforce a child execution timeout (kill on expiry), bounded stdout/stderr buffers, and `MAX_FILE_BYTES` output size limit (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/mod.rs`).
- Execute `cadmpeg check --json <input>` and `cadmpeg convert <input> -o <step_out> --to step --reject-lossy=export` without `--allow-errors`. Refuse nonzero exits, blocking findings, or empty outputs by name.
- Pass converted STEP output into `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs` (`step::parse_open`) and all existing STEP guards (`step_depth`, `step_edge3d`, `step_closed::closed_shells`, `step_guard`, `step_refine`, `step_outward`).
- Replace the hardcoded `"iges" | "igs"` `CommandError::UnsupportedType` arm in `ImportModel::checked_budget` (`crates/app/src/commands/import_model.rs`) with routing through the shared qualified-extension table. Keep the table empty until format qualification enables passing formats, and refuse unqualified extensions such as `L1` `.prt` by name.
- Add desktop unit tests using stub executables for success, missing binary, old version, nonzero `cadmpeg check`, timeout cleanup, oversized STEP refusal, and garbage output without touching `Cargo.toml` dependencies.

## Done means
`camcraft-app` resolves `cadmpeg`, enforces version `>= 0.6.12`, converts in a cleaned temp dir with timeout and size caps, refuses `check` errors by name, feeds output into `step::parse_open`, and passes stub-binary tests without new `Cargo.toml` crates.

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

Depends on #1860.

## Goal
Chain 2D sketch primitives within a caller tolerance in `crates/geometry/` into deterministic closed loops and open chains, classify outer loops vs holes, and enforce open-chain safety.

## Scope
- Take normalized 2D primitives (`Line`, `Arc`, `Circle`, `Polyline`) and layer names from #1860 together with a configurable join tolerance in millimeters (default `0.01` mm).
- Join touching endpoints that lie within the join tolerance into connected chains. Never bridge gaps wider than the tolerance.
- Keep original `Arc` and `Circle` segment metadata inside each chain so downstream CAM operations emit true `G2`/`G3` arcs where possible.
- Assign each chain a stable geometry-hash `ChainId` derived from its quantized curve geometry and layer name.
- Separate closed chains from open chains explicitly. Report open endpoints and never close an open chain silently.
- Resolve closed chain nesting into outer boundaries vs inner holes using `geo2d::Region` / `clipper2-rust` winding rules.
- Reject self-crossing closed loops and degenerate chains with clear named errors instead of panicking.
- Handle T-junctions or branching vertices cleanly with deterministic traversal or named diagnostics.

## Done means
Tests chain unordered lines, arcs, and circles into stable `ChainId` loops and open chains within a specified tolerance; gaps wider than tolerance remain explicitly open; nested rectangles and circles classify accurately as outer loops vs holes; self-crossing loops return a named error; arc metadata survives chaining.

labels.name: enhancement

body:
Maintainer request from #1452 ("We should be able to load DXF file to do profile cuts on.").

## Goal
Build a clean-room ASCII DXF reader in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/`. Read Autodesk's published DXF Reference only. Add zero new external crate dependencies. Keep the API neutral so #743 and #744 can share it later.

## Scope
- Parse DXF sections `HEADER`, `TABLES`, and `ENTITIES`.
- Read `$INSUNITS` explicitly as `Known(Unit)` (inch code `1`, millimeter code `4`, plus standard length scales), `MissingOrUnitless` (`0` or absent), or `Unsupported(i32)`. Never guess millimeters vs inches on missing units.
- Read `LAYER` definitions and keep layer names on every extracted primitive.
- Parse 2D primitives `LINE`, `ARC`, `CIRCLE`, `LWPOLYLINE`, and `POLYLINE`/`VERTEX`/`SEQEND`. Convert group-42 bulges into exact `Arc` segments and keep `ARC` and `CIRCLE` exact without polygonizing.
- Skip `TEXT`, `MTEXT`, `DIMENSION`, and `HATCH`, and count skipped entities per kind in an import summary struct.
- Reject non-planar extrusion vectors (`210`, `220`, `230` tilted away from `+Z`) or varying Z heights by name.
- Guard untrusted input strictly: detect and refuse Binary DXF (`AutoCAD Binary DXF`) headers, enforce maximum file size, entity count, and vertex count caps before bulk allocation, reject NaN/Inf or coordinates past `geo2d::COORD_LIMIT`, drop or refuse zero-length entities safely, and use zero `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`.
- Leave `SPLINE`, `ELLIPSE`, and `BLOCK`/`INSERT` to the follow-up curve/block sub-issue, refusing them by DXF entity name for now.

## Done means
Tests parse valid ASCII DXFs with rectangles, circles, arcs, bulges, layers, and `$INSUNITS` into exact primitives; tests refuse binary files, malformed group codes, truncated streams, unsupported entities, tilted extrusions, NaN values, and oversized counts by name; a deterministic smoke-fuzz test runs with zero panics.

body:
## What we found

The work on issue 1715 (split of the `shared_face_bodies` 3D Finish test) found this. The test job has two operations: the 3D Pocket `R1` and the 3D Finish `S1`. The test generates `S1` only. `R1` stays at status `never`.

Thus the verify gate does not run. The `verify` reply has:

```
"gate":{"ok":false,"problems":[],"skipped":"an operation is stale or never generated - regenerate before judging the program"}
```

The test asserts that no entry of `gate.problems` starts with `gouge`. The list is always empty, so the assert checks nothing. This was true for the old whole-span test `the_sample_as_imported_still_generates_the_3d_finish` too. The new band tests in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies_finish.rs` keep the same assert, because the split must not change an assert.

The same `verify` reply also has `"held_by":["S1"]` and many `S1` warnings of this type:

```
shank/holder at move 181 collides with the part or an island
shank/holder at move 1452 collides with the uncut stock
```

Band 1 (top) has 273 findings, band 5 has 2587. The post is held, so the output is not silent. But no test asserts on these collisions.

## What to do

1. Make the no-gouge assert real: delete `R1` from the job of the band tests (or generate it, if #1749 makes it generate), so that the stock sim runs. Then assert `gate.problems` has no `gouge` entry.
2. Find out if the shank/holder collisions of `S1` on the as-imported sample are correct. If they are correct, pin them by name. If they are wrong, file a defect.

## Done means

The band tests run the verify gate (`gate.skipped` is absent) and assert on its result.

title: Carry machined stock side-on exactly: remove the one-cell over-read on turned faces

labels.name: enhancement

labels.name: P7

body:
Part of #874. Found while working #874 (PR #1804). Related: #637, #589, #321.

**What happens now.** PR #1804 carries the machined stock through a side-on quarter turn with a conservative read of the column body (`Body::carry_side`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/carry_side.rs`). The carried stock is never smaller than the real stock. The cost is this:

- A wall that the tool flank cut, or a step, is read up to one grid cell outside the real face after the turn.
- A cavity seen from the side (a pocket of the earlier setup) is filled.
- The field engine refuses a side-on turn by name (`FIELD_SIDE_CARRY_REFUSAL`).

**What a user can see.**

- The verdict can show rest of up to one cell on a face that is finished.
- The carried-fixture law (#321, `fixture_carried.rs`) can refuse a fixture that touches a turned face that was machined. The workaround is the setup's own stock.
- Rest machining in the turned setup can cut air in a filled cavity.

**The work.** Carry the stock side-on with the wall positions the engine knows, not the column pitch. One path is the field engine: re-index its 3-D bricks through the full signed permutation (`field_turn.rs` has the lattice turns only) and give it a column read that does not assume cuts along Z (`column_span`, `cut_ups`, `cut_downs`). The decision record `docs/decisions/874-side-on-carry.md` lists what was considered.

**Rule that stays.** The carried stock is never smaller than the real stock. A turn that the engine cannot carry is refused by name.

**Done means:** a plate with a contoured wall is carried side-on and the turned wall is read within the verdict tolerance, not one cell outside; a fixture in contact with that wall is not refused; a pocket of the earlier setup is still a cavity after the turn; a pinning test checks all three, and the field engine no longer refuses the side-on turn (or the issue says why it must).

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**The request (the user, 2026-11-14):** "create an ai chat window in CamCraft that would interact with ai thru mcp or whatever appropriate. Make sure that we help those agents with appropriate skill stuff for various ai tools like Claude, codex, Gemini, unsloth, ollama, etc."

This is a research umbrella (`needs-research`). It answers the open questions below in comments. Then it files the concrete sub-issues and closes. No code goes on this issue.

## What exists today

- `camcraft-cli mcp` is an MCP server on stdio. An agent drives one headless document.
- The app can start with `--mcp-port`, and `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` bridges an external agent to the open window. The agent then drives the live document.
- The skill `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/` documents the tools for Claude Code.
- Every MCP tool calls the same undoable commands as the GUI (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Goal

1. **In-app chat panel.** A dock panel in CamCraft where the user types a request, for example "add a 2D pocket on the selected face with T3". An AI model answers and acts through the same MCP tool set. The panel shows each tool call and its result.
2. **Provider choice.** The user picks the model provider and the model:
   - **Cloud:** Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT/Codex models), Google (Gemini).
   - **Local:** Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp server (most local servers have an OpenAI-compatible API).
3. **External agents.** Each external agent tool gets one documented way to drive the open app (`--mcp-port` plus `mcp --connect`), and a skill or instruction file in its own format:
   - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/` (exists; keep it current);
   - Codex CLI: AGENTS.md section or `.codex/` instructions;
   - Gemini / Antigravity CLI: `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/skills/`;
   - local models through Ollama or Unsloth: a short system prompt plus the tool list.

## Open questions (answer each in a comment)

1. **Panel architecture.** In-process, where the app calls the provider API and maps the MCP tools to the provider's tool-calling format? Or a separate process that speaks MCP to the app? What keeps the UI thread free (async, cancel)?
2. **One tool schema for all providers.** Map the MCP tool schemas to the Anthropic Messages tool format, the OpenAI tools format, and Gemini function declarations. Which local models do tool calling well enough? What is the fallback for a model without tool calling?
3. **Safety.**
   - Every action goes through the undoable commands.
   - The chat never posts G-code, never writes a file, and never changes a machine without a confirmation in the panel.
   - Group one chat turn as one undo step, or one step per command?
   - How does the panel show what changed?
4. **Keys and privacy.**
   - Where do API keys live (the OS keychain)?
   - What is sent to a cloud model (the project data, the model geometry)?
   - How does an offline-only setting work (local models only)?
5. **Context size.** How does a large project (many operations, big meshes) fit a model's context window? Summaries, on-demand tool reads?
6. **Skills per tool.** One source of truth for the tool docs (generated from the MCP tool list?) with per-tool wrappers, so the docs never drift from the shipped tools.
7. **Tests.** Test the panel and the tool mapping without network access (a scripted fake provider).
8. **Clean room.** Only public API documentation of each provider and the MCP specification. No code or prompts copied from other CAM products.

## Sub-issues to file (when the research is done)

- The chat panel: UI, history, tool-call display, cancel, confirmation prompts.
- The provider adapters: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible local (Ollama, Unsloth, LM Studio, llama.cpp).
- The tool-schema mapping, generated from the MCP tool list.
- Keys and privacy settings, plus the offline mode.
- Skill and instruction files for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity and local models, generated from one source.
- Docs (REQUIRED): "Use AI with CamCraft": setup and worked examples for every provider (Claude, OpenAI/Codex, Gemini, Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and every external agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini/Antigravity CLI, headless). See the comment that adds docs to the scope.

**Done means:** every open question has an answered comment, every sub-issue is filed with "Part of #this", and this umbrella is closed.

title: Mask tests: compare a generated toolpath with its described shape

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat (2026-11-15):

> is it possible to use the cli tool to verify tool paths "visually".. we know what they should look like mathematically.. could we inspect them using rasterized tests?

> Idea is to sanity checks that changes to the motion crates actually gets implemented as described by the user

## Problem

A change to a toolpath generator is described in words in its issue (for example "the pass extends to the stock edge", "the corners are arcs", "the slot is cleared with trochoidal loops"). The tests of the change pin numbers that the author chose. No test compares the shape of the generated toolpath with the shape that the description gives. A change can pass its tests and not do what the user described.

## Proposal

Add a test helper that compares two masks on one grid:

- The expected region. The test builds it from the mathematical description (an outline, a depth, an extension).
- The swept region. The helper builds it from the tool footprint along the generated toolpath.

The helper gives these assertions:

- No overcut: no swept cell is outside the expected region, within one cell.
- Bounded leftover: the uncut area is below a stated limit, and the uncut cells are only in stated places.
- Engagement: no move cuts a width larger than the stated stepover.
- Shape laws: symmetry for a symmetric region, and no move outside the stock plus the stated extension.

When an assertion fails, the helper writes the difference mask as a PNG file into the test output folder. A person can then see where the toolpath is wrong. The test result comes from the numbers, not from an image comparison. No PNG golden is stored.

## Rules

- The helper is test code. It does not change a generator, a gouge check or a collision check.
- The helper is in the crate that owns the toolpath types (`crates/motion`), and uses the CPU rasteriser or its own grid. It does not need a GPU.
- The grid limits the precision to one cell. Exact laws (arc radius, depth, feed words) stay as numeric tests.
- A PR that changes a 2D generator in `crates/motion` adds or updates one mask test that states the described shape.

## First users

- Trochoidal slot.
- 2D Adaptive.
- The open-edge region of issue 1735 and the Slot extension of issue 1731.

Done means: the helper is in the repository with its own unit tests; the trochoidal slot and 2D Adaptive each have one mask test that fails when the generator is changed to overcut or to leave too much material (shown by a mutation check in the PR); a failed assertion writes the difference PNG; AGENTS.md "Testing" names the helper.

body:
**What happens.** A whole-model 3D Pocket clears a notch that is open to the part's outside: a quadrant step in the side of a block. It leaves tall ridges of stock along the part's outer edge at the notch, because the cutter stays inside the model boundary. The op reports `ok`. The next setup then refuses the post, correctly: `fixture '…' stands inside the stock carried from setup 'Setup 1' (9.93 mm deep)`.

**Numbers (CamCraft v0.20.0, a user's two-sided part).**
- The part is a 30 mm cube made of two L halves, with R3.125 fillets. Setup 1 cuts the top notch with a 3D Pocket: whole model, shell on, offset rings, a 6.35 mm flat end mill, 2.032 mm stepover, 0.15 mm stepdown, 0 stock to leave. The floor is Z 19.826.
- In the middle of the notch, the carried stock is cut to the floor, as expected.
- Near the notch's open edges (for example X 14.81 at the part edge), the carried stock stays at Z 33.326 and 34.676, about 14-15 mm above the floor. The finished model there is at about Z 18-19.
- The flip into Setup 2 and the fixture positions are correct. The fixtures clear the finished model by 1.0 to 3.6 mm. The carried-stock check measures the uncut ridge correctly.

**Expected.** Either the pocket clears an open-sided notch to the part's outer edge (the open side is air, so the cutter may go past the model boundary into the stock), or the op says by name that it leaves material along an open edge, and how much.

**Workaround today.** A machining boundary or a stock-source region that reaches past the part's edge at the open sides. Not yet tested.

**Done means:** a 3D Pocket on a block with an open-sided quadrant notch leaves no material above the floor plus the stock to leave at the open edges, pinned by a test. Or the op names the material it leaves.

title: web/build-app-wasm.sh fails to link on stock macOS: Apple's ar leaves the flecs wasm archive empty

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Follow-up to #1315 (PR #1485), tested on macOS 27 (Apple silicon) with `/bin/bash` 3.2 and BSD sed at `0b4052bb`.

**What happens:** after #1485, the script gets through the sysroot download, the `shasum` check and the `sed` patching on macOS. The link of `camcraft-cli` then fails with `rust-lld: error: … undefined symbol: ecs_has_id` (and `ecs_modified_id`, `ecs_cpp_set`, …). The `cc` crate archives the flecs C objects with Apple's `/usr/bin/ar` and `ranlib`, which only handle Mach-O. The flecs build warns `ranlib: warning: archive member 'flecs_rust.o' not a mach-o file`, and `libflecs.a` comes out at 96 bytes.

**Confirmed fix:** with `AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar`, the archive is 2.1 MB, the script finishes, and `web/check-app-page.sh target/web` passes. `git status` stays clean.

**Suggested change:** on macOS, when `AR_wasm32_unknown_unknown` isn't set, the script finds `llvm-ar` (on PATH, Homebrew's `$(brew --prefix llvm)/bin`, or rustup's `llvm-tools`) and exports it. With none found, it stops with a message naming what to install (`brew install llvm` or `rustup component add llvm-tools`) instead of failing at the link. "Needs:" in the header gains `llvm-ar` on macOS.

**Done means:** #1315's own definition of done. `web/build-app-wasm.sh` and `web/check-app-page.sh` run unmodified on macOS with `/bin/bash` and BSD sed.

title: 2D ops cannot start below the material top: the entry rapids into uncut stock, so the air pass at Top cannot be avoided

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical output**.

## What happens

Every 2D depth ladder cuts its first level at `top_z` (#514, kept by the maintainer on 2026-11-11). When Top is the faced material top, that level is a full pass in air. The obvious way to avoid it, setting Top to the first real cut, is **refused**: the entry rapids straight down to Top + the plunge height, which is inside the uncut stock above Top, and verify convicts it:

`rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock`

So the air pass cannot be avoided. In the user's project the bore adaptive (2D Adaptive, three 0.25 in levels) keeps an air level at the faced top: **about 5.6 of its 16.9 min**.

Repro (main and v0.19.0 alike), a plate in stock 0.5 mm taller, faced to the part top first, `stepdown: 4`, bottom at the part bottom:

| op | `top_z` | levels (z) | first moves | verify |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2D Adaptive (bore) | TOS -0.5 (faced top) | 10 (air), 6, 2, 0 | rapid to z 12, feed down | ok |
| 2D Adaptive (bore) | TOS -4.5 | 6, 2, 0 | **rapid to z 8** (stock is at z 10) | `rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock` |
| 2D Contour inside (bore) | TOS -0.5 | 10 (air), 6, 2, 0 | rapid to z 12, plunge | ok |
| 2D Contour inside (bore) | TOS -4.5 | 6, 2, 0 | **rapid to z 8** | same message, moves 1 and 5 |

The rapid law is right to convict a rapid into stock; the generator is what puts it there.

## Minimal repro (MCP)

`plate_bore.stl`: a 100 x 60 x 10 mm plate, centred, z 0..10, with a centred Ø40 through bore.

```
import_model   {"path": "plate_bore.stl", "name": "plate"}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 70, "dz": 10.5}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "EM6"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Face", "tool": "EM6", "name": "face", "params": {"cut_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -0.5}}}
add_operation  {"kind": "2D Adaptive", "tool": "EM6", "name": "op", "source": "plate",
                "params": {"top_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -4.5},
                           "bottom_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -10.5}, "stepdown": 4}}
set_operation_geometry {"operation": "op", "picks": [the bore's top chain]}
generate {} ; verify {}  -> "rapid move 1 travels below the clearance plane inside stock"
```

## Expected

An op whose Top is below the material standing over it enters safely: it rapids to the plunge height above the **material actually there** (the prior stock, or the stock top), then feeds (helix, ramp or plunge) down to its first level. Then a user can set Top to the first real cut and skip the air pass, without reopening the #514 ladder decision.

## Done means

- The repro above (Adaptive and Contour, Top 4 mm below the faced top) generates an entry that rapids no lower than the plunge height above the remaining material and feeds the rest; verify is clean; pinned by a test for each.
- The rapid law (#96, #1066, #1091 pins) is unchanged.

Related: #514 (the air level at Top, won't-do for now), #1066.

title: Through holes run a hidden, fixed 1.0 mm past the part bottom, not a parameter and not checked against what is under the part

labels.name: bug

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still the same**.

## What happens

`detect_holes` reports a through hole with `"floor_z"` at the part bottom and `"through": true`. At generation the Bore (and Drill/Thread) path then goes a further **1.0 mm** below that floor: the hard-coded `THROUGH_CLEAR = 1.0` in `crates/motion/src/drilling/hole.rs`, passed as `through_allowance` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`.

- The 1.0 mm is not a parameter. It is not shown on the op, in the hole list or in `get_job`, and cannot be changed (the only way is to set `through: false` and type a deeper floor by hand, which is what the user did).
- It is not tied to anything under the part: not the stock bottom, a HAT web, the parallels or the setup. In the repro the part bottom is z 4.826 and the path goes to z 3.826 (the stock bottom is z 0). With the part bottom on the stock bottom, it cuts 1 mm below the stock, into whatever the part sits on, with no note (the fixture laws may catch a modelled parallel; an unmodelled table or spoilboard is not judged).
- It is in mm whatever the document units (an inch user would choose 0.020-0.040 in, and might want it scaled to the tool's tip, e.g. a drill's point length).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Bore", "tool": "EM4", "name": "Bore", "source": "part", "params": {"stepdown": 2.0}}
detect_holes   {"name": "Bore"}   -> every hole "floor_z": 4.826, "through": true
generate {}                       -> deepest feed z 3.826, no note
```

## Expected

- The break-through is a visible, editable op parameter (default 1.0 mm or a tool-relative value), in document units, saved with the project and settable over MCP.
- The op says what it did (a note: "through holes run 1.0 mm past the part bottom, to z ...").
- The depth past the part is checked against what is under it: never below the stock bottom unless the user allows it, and refused by name if it would reach a fixture.

## Done means

- A through-hole break-through parameter on Drill, Bore and Thread (GUI field, project file, MCP `params`), with a default equal to today's 1.0 mm so existing goldens hold.
- The generated note states the break-through depth; a through hole whose break-through would go below the stock bottom is noted or refused; pinned by tests.

Related: #1556 (large bores in hole detection).

title: Setup WCS Z as the tool direction for a milling setup (reference behaviour; maintainer to decide)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Found while triaging issue 1510 (maintainer asked for a check against published references, 2026-11-13).

What we do today: a milling setup always cuts along the machine's Z as the model lies. The part is turned for a setup with Part alignment (issue 326). A WCS tilted off Z is refused at generation by name (PR 1518).

What the published documentation of the product we reimplement describes (behaviour only, read through a search summary, not verified page by page):
- The setup's WCS orientation sets the default tool direction: pointing the WCS Z out of another face makes that setup's 3-axis toolpaths cut from that direction; the model is not turned. The operator flips the part on the machine to match.
  - https://help.autodesk.com/cloudhelp/ENU/Fusion-CAM/files/MFG-TOOL-ORIENTATION-OVERVIEW.htm
  - https://www.autodesk.com/products/fusion-360/blog/fusion-360-wcs-tool-orientation/
- G54-G59 are translations on the machine (LinuxCNC also allows a rotation about Z); they do not re-aim the spindle: https://linuxcnc.org/docs/html/gcode/coordinates.html

So the reporter of 1510 used the workflow that documentation teaches. The maintainer's stated view (2026-11-13, in chat) is the opposite design: "You should orient the part to Z using Setup.. Not let the WCS orient the part to Z..". Both give the same posted program for a flipped part; they differ in which control the user turns.

To decide (maintainer):
1. Keep Part alignment as the only way to turn a part (today). Then the WCS pane should not offer a tilt for a milling setup, or should offer "turn the part with Part alignment" at that moment, so a user coming from the reference product is led there before Generate refuses.
2. Or let a tilted setup WCS define the tool direction (generate in the WCS frame; `docs/decisions/1510-tilted-wcs.md` rated that effort:max: every generator, stock, heights, simulation and the post's rotated-offset refusal are involved).

Safety: whichever is chosen, a tilted WCS never generates a path in a frame other than the one shown; the refusal of PR 1518 stays until option 2 is complete.

Done means: the maintainer's choice is recorded here; for option 1, the WCS pane change with its structural test; for option 2, sub-issues filed and this one closed as the umbrella.

Decided by the maintainer (2026-11-13). His question in chat: "Should we have "both" 2D pocket with the strategy of adaptive making one type of path - and 2D Adaptive ... both might have its purpose - but its confusing to the user which does what.. Trochoidal should land on 2D and 3D Adaptives to start with tho (see issues)". Answer in the question dialog: "Adaptive op only".

What is confusing today: 2D Pocket offers an Adaptive strategy (`PocketStrategy` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_strategy.rs`) and there is also a separate 2D Adaptive operation. Both run the same adaptive planner, so two places make the same kind of cut with different pages.

- A project saved with 2D Pocket + Adaptive opens as a 2D Adaptive operation with the same parameters and generates the same toolpath (no silent change of what is cut). If a parameter cannot be carried, the operation opens marked "needs review" and names it; it never posts a different path without saying so.
- The MCP tools and script verbs follow: the Pocket strategy value is refused by name with a pointer to 2D Adaptive, or mapped the same way as the project file.

Rules: one planner, one home per kind of cut; a project-file change that older builds cannot read is a breaking change and says so.

Done means: Pocket's strategy list has no Adaptive; an old project with Pocket+Adaptive reopens as 2D Adaptive with an identical golden CL; 2D and 3D Adaptive show a Method choice (Trochoidal may land with issue 1509); undo/redo; MCP parameters; structural UI test updated.

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "we should be able to set start points on generated path and also exit points.. So the path gets regenerated to those."

What is missing: where an operation starts cutting and where it leaves is chosen by the generator alone. The user cannot say "enter here" or "leave here", for example to keep the entry mark off a visible face, to start a contour away from a clamp, or to end next to the following feature.

Wanted: on the operations where it has a meaning (2D Contour, Pocket, Adaptive, Face, Slot, Bore, and the 3D finishing passes that have a free start), two optional picks:
- Start point(s): picked in the viewport (a point on the model, a sketch point or typed coordinates). For a closed contour the path is re-sequenced to begin at the pick's nearest point on the chain, with its lead-in there; for a pocket or adaptive region the entry (helix, ramp or plunge) is placed at the pick. One pick per chain or region; chains with no pick keep the automatic choice.
- Exit point(s): the same for where the pass ends and the lead-out is placed.

Changing a pick is an undoable command (it edits the operation parameters) and regenerates the path. MCP: the same parameters on the operation tools.

Safety: a pick is a wish, never an override of a check. If the entry, lead or ramp at the picked place does not fit (helix does not fit in the region, lead-in gouges a wall, the point is outside the machinable region or inside a keep-out or fixture), the operation is refused by name or marked incomplete, saying which pick and why; it never moves the entry silently and never posts a path that the collision or gouge checks would refuse at the automatic entry.

Related: the companion issue on pre-drilled holes as entry positions (filed with this one).

Done means: a closed 2D contour with a picked start begins and leads in at that point and, with a picked exit, leads out there (golden CL); a pocket enters at its picked point; an impossible pick is refused by name in a test; undo and redo restore the previous path; the MCP tools take the picks; the structural UI test covers the two pick rows.

body:
Part of #290. Found while building #537 (4-axis upper/lower profiles).

**What happens now.** A straight wire cannot touch a twisted (non-developable) ruled surface along its whole height. #537 keeps the kerf out by widening the kerf offset on both profile planes *uniformly* until the leaning kerf stands clear at every height read, and refuses past the op's `four_axis.tolerance`. Two costs follow:

1. The whole profile stands the widening proud of the kerf offset, though only the twisted stretches (e.g. the corners of a square-to-round) need it.
2. The wire laws (`sim::verify::wire`) judge the *mesh* with a 0.1 um tolerance. A model whose tessellation of a twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface between the two picked profiles (any STEP loft tessellated at a chord tolerance) is refused as a gouge - safe, but it blocks a correct cut of a real model.

**Wanted.**
- Widen per ruling (a variable offset along the profiles, with its own corner law) so the standing stock is only where the twist is; the path's note states the worst.
- A stated verify tolerance for a 4-axis cut (the op's own, visible on the report line) against which the wire laws judge the tessellated wall - never silent, never a default that hides a gouge.

Evidence: `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled.rs` (uniform widening), `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`; the #537 fixture meshes are split along the inner diagonal so they stand inside the ruled surface.

**Done means:** a square-to-round punch stands at the kerf offset on its straight stretches and widened only at the twist (pinned by a motion test reading both), and a lofted model tessellated at a stated chord tolerance posts when the op states a verify tolerance at least that large and is refused by name when it does not (pinned by an app test).

title: Reduced-fidelity models: swarf's flank proof reads the excess, so swarf is judged instead of refused

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Part of #904. Found while working #904: swarf is the one multi-axis family still refused on a reduced-fidelity model.

**What is owed.** A swarf tool cuts with its flank. That the flank stands clear of the wall is proved only inside the generator (`motion` `multiaxis/stamp_pose.rs` and `stamp_rise.rs`, through `stamp_link::flank_clear` at the plan tolerance). No verify law re-measures it: law (f) judges the ball, and the reach laws judge the bands above the flute. So on a model imported coarser than promised there is no verdict to tighten, and `operation::fidelity_law::excess_aware` keeps Swarf and Advanced Swarf refused at the program gate.

Two ways to close it, to be decided by whoever takes it:

1. Thread the model's excess into the flank proof (`Ruled::tol` as `flank_clear` reads it), so the generator proves clearance with the tightened tolerance. This changes the paths generated on a reduced-fidelity model.
2. Add a verify law that measures the flank against the part, and tighten that. Larger, but it would also judge the flank at full fidelity, where today only the generator speaks.

**Done means:** Swarf and Advanced Swarf on a reduced-fidelity model are judged while a positive tolerance is left (and refused by name past that), with a pin for a flank cut between the tightened and the plain tolerance; or the refusal stays with the reason recorded in `docs/decisions`.

Part of #361.

**What happens.** A tool carries one body from one file. Modular tooling is sold and modelled in pieces: a clamping unit or basic holder on the turret or spindle, an adapter, a cutting head, the insert - joined at standardised interfaces (the issue names ISO 26622 and ISO 26623 polygon/taper couplings). Vendors publish one STEP per piece, so today the user must merge them in a CAD system before importing.

**Open design.** How a tool's body becomes a stack of placed pieces (each a file with its own placement relative to the one below), how the pieces mate (by the coordinate systems the files name, or by numbers), what the laws read (the union: one envelope for a spindle body, one set of clearance bands for a lathe body), and how it is saved. Only public documentation of the interface standards may be used; no vendor file is committed.

**Done means:** two synthetic pieces (our own STEPs) are attached to one tool, placed against each other, judged as one body, saved and reloaded; removing one piece is one undo step.

labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P8
labels.description: Larger idea needing design or research before code

body:
Follow-up of #940 (machining mesh seam, PR stacked on #941).

What #940 delivers: `camcraft_kernel::machining_mesh` refuses by name every `PlanStats` shortfall that touches the guarantee (unmeshed, lenient, unsampled edge, a face or edge capped off its tolerance), pinned by `every_planner_shortfall_is_a_refusal_or_a_note` on SYNTHETIC `PlanStats` values; and a SAMPLED deviation (15 barycentric points a triangle), judged by the closed-form distance to the record's analytic surface where the face is analytic, else by the parametric distance |S(u,v) - T(u,v)|.

Owed:
1. **Real provocations.** No fixture under testdata/models makes the planner report any shortfall (checked at 0.005, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0002 and 0.0001 mm on Milling-test.step and sample_ap214.step). Build small crafted records (a pcurve off its edge, a free edge, a face whose grid must be thinned past `MAX_FACE_GRID`, an edge past 20 000 nodes) and pin that each reaches its named `MeshRefusal` through `machining_mesh`, not only through `judge_stats`.
2. **Spline and revolved faces.** They are judged only by the parametric distance, which over-reads on a non-uniform parameterisation (a few per cent on a rational circle) - a possible false refusal. Add a projection onto the plan surface (Newton from the sample's (u, v)) so they get a true distance, with a fixture that has such a face.
3. **Between the samples.** The deviation is a sampled maximum, a lower bound of the true one; solidcore-tess meshes right up to the tolerance (0.993 of it on Milling-test). Either a stated bound on the sag between samples, or a margin in the seam, so "within" is a guarantee.

What upstream solidcore-tess would need (for the maintainer to raise; not filed upstream): a cancellation hook in `plan`; a per-face measured sag in `PlanStats` for every face; a stated bound on the sag between the planner's sample points.

Everything stays inside `crates/kernel`. Part of #27. Gates #917.

Done means: each shortfall entry is pinned by a crafted record through `machining_mesh`; a non-analytic face is judged by a projected distance with a fixture; the decision file says what bounds the sag between samples.

title: Adaptive plans differ across platforms on the same commit (likely libm last-place rounding)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Found while working #984.

**What happens:** the same commit plans the same part differently on two platforms. `app pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (release) on ecb54b7f:

| platform | rings levels | moves / planar / arcs |
|---|---|---|
| Windows (the #850 measure, PR #865) | Z 20.000 | 5530 / 5497 / 600 |
| macOS, Apple silicon (Homebrew rustc 1.99.1) | Z 20.000 (crossing at -2.33, -2.78) | 5786 / 5753 / 651 |

macOS is deterministic run to run, so it is not hash-map order. Rust does not contract `a*b+c` into FMA unless asked, so the most likely cause is the platform libm: `f64::sin`, `cos`, `atan2`, `hypot`, `exp`, `powf` call the system math library (MSVC CRT, glibc, Apple libm), which are not correctly rounded and differ in the last place. The STEP tessellation and the adaptive planner both use them, and the planner's crossing and acceptance tests are knife edges a 16 nm change flips (#882, #982). Not yet confirmed which call sites diverge, and not run on Linux.

**Why it matters:** a toolpath (and so the posted G-code) for the same part, tool and parameters depends on the OS the user runs. Every output is still verified and a crossing plan is refused by name, so this is not a gouge; but golden counts and exact plan pins cannot hold across platforms, and a user can see a different path from the same project file on two machines.

**Possible directions (open):** route the geometry and planner transcendental calls through a pure-Rust deterministic libm (the `libm` crate is already in Cargo.lock) so every platform rounds the same; or make the planner's decisions robust to sub-micron perturbation (#882, #982). Either changes toolpaths and needs every adaptive fixture re-measured.

Done means: the cause is confirmed on a second platform (Windows or Linux run of the bore test, plus which calls diverge), and either the output is made platform-identical with goldens re-measured, or the decision not to is recorded.

Refs #984, #882, #982.

title: Build cycle: every worktree compiles the whole dependency tree cold - share a compile cache, cut debug info, use a faster linker

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
Raised by the maintainer (2026-11-11): "why are we cold building complete bundles .. the tests are localized to crates".

## What happens today (measured on the dev machine)
- Every issue worker, reviewer and gate works in its own worktree with its own `target/`. A fresh one compiles the WHOLE dependency tree before the first test runs: about 15-25 minutes per review and 25-75 minutes per gate, almost all of it third-party crates (flecs' C through bindgen/cc, wgpu/egui, the B-rep kernel, the script engine ...), not our code.
- `Cargo.toml` sets `[profile.dev.package."*"] opt-level = 2`: every dependency is optimised in dev builds. That makes tests run faster but makes each cold build much slower.
- Nothing sets `debug`, so dev builds carry full debug info for all crates: one `target/` reaches 50-120 GB (the disk filled twice today) and every link is slow.
- Integration tests are one binary per file: `crates/app/tests` has 266 files, motion 65, sim 50. The batch gate's app step takes about 24 of its 38 minutes, much of it linking and starting 266 binaries.
- `.cargo/config.toml` holds only the `xtask` alias: no linker choice, no cache wrapper. `sccache` is not installed; `rust-lld` is.

## Wanted (this issue: the three cheap ones, measured)
1. **A shared compile cache across worktrees** (`sccache` as `RUSTC_WRAPPER`, and as the C compiler wrapper for the cc-built C code if that works on MSVC). Registry crates live at the same path for every worktree, so their compilations are cache hits; a fresh worktree should then compile only our own crates. It must be OPTIONAL: a machine without sccache builds exactly as today (enable it from `cargo xtask` / the gate wrappers when `sccache` is on PATH, or document the env var - never hard-code a wrapper in `.cargo/config.toml` that breaks a machine without it). Say how to install it and how big its cache is allowed to grow.
2. **Less debug info**: `debug = false` (or `"line-tables-only"`) for dependencies, and line tables only for our crates in dev/test - enough for backtraces and panics with file:line. Report target size and link time before/after.
3. **A faster linker** for the Windows MSVC target (`rust-lld` / `lld-link`), and the equivalent on Linux/macOS where it helps, again without breaking a machine that lacks it.
4. Re-examine `opt-level = 2` for all dependencies: keep it only for the crates whose speed the tests need (measure: batch gate time with opt-level 2 everywhere vs 1 vs a short list).

Measure and report, on the same machine, cold (empty target, warm cache where a cache applies) and warm: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --no-run`, `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test <one binary>`, `cargo xtask gate quick` on a one-file app change, and the `target/` size. No test may change behaviour; the gates stay green.

## Not in this issue (file separately if the numbers say so)
- Folding the 266 one-file app test binaries into a few binaries (one per area, files as modules). This is the biggest structural win for the gate, but it changes the gate maps in `xtask` and every "run this binary" instruction.

## Process
`.cargo/config.toml`, `xtask/` and the gate wrappers are process files: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, and say in the PR what a fork must do.

Done means: a fresh worktree reaches its first app test at least 3x faster than today with the cache warm, `target/` is at most half today's size, the settings are optional per machine and documented, and the measured numbers are in the PR.

body:
Hole-making tools beyond the twist drill have no kind, and drills get no feeds-and-speeds suggestion.

**Where:**
- `ToolKind` has `Drill` only: no reamer, spot drill, countersink or combined center drill.
- `tabulated()` (`crates/app/src/cutting.rs:41`) excludes `Drill`, so CamCraft suggests no feeds for any drill.

**Effect:**
- A reamer can't be stored with its semantics: no chamfer lead, finish allowance, or slower speed.
- Spot drills are stored as drills, so their geometry is right but there's no "spot to a chamfer diameter" behaviour.
- No drill gets a starting rpm/feed from the cutting table.

**Fix sketch:**
- Reamer, spot drill, countersink and center drill kinds, with their op behaviours: ream at a reduced speed with a set allowance; spot or countersink to a stated diameter.
- Drill rows in the cutting table: feed per rev by diameter and material, as conservative handbook-range values.

Effort: high.

**Done means:** a reamer and a spot drill can be stored and used with their behaviour; drills get a suggested rpm/feed; pinned.
